1.meaning: A two-part expression: an emphatic particle that strongly affirms and confirms a statement ('truly, indeed, certainly'), fused with the attached pronoun 'we.' Together: 'truly we…' / 'indeed we…'
1.grammar: The particle inna gives strong emphasis and certainty to the clause it opens. The attached -ā is the pronoun 'we,' serving as the subject being emphasized: 'truly we…'

2.meaning: A verb meaning 'we opened' or 'we unlocked/laid open.' The root conveys opening, granting access, or beginning; it can also mean to grant victory or to judge/decide between parties.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -nā ending marks 'we' as the doers of a completed action.
2.root: ف-ت-ح (f-t-ḥ) — to open, grant, decide, give victory

3.meaning: 'For You / to You' — a 'for/to' particle attached to the pronoun 'You,' indicating that something is directed toward, or done for the sake of, a single addressee.
3.grammar: A small phrase: the particle li- ('for / to,' vowelled la- before a pronoun) joined to the attached pronoun -ka, 'you' (one masculine addressee). The pronoun is in the form used as the object of a preposition, marking the person as the one to whom or for whom the action is directed.
3.root: — (particle + pronoun, no triliteral root)

4.meaning: A clear, manifest opening or victory — a decisive triumph that removes an obstacle and opens the way forward. In Qur'anic usage it denotes a victory granted by Allah that unfolds with clarity and completeness.
4.grammar: Indefinite masculine noun in the accusative case (manṣūb), marked by tanwīn fatḥ (-an). Serves as the object of the implied verb or predicate complement.
4.root: ف-ت-ح (f-t-ḥ) — to open, to conquer, to grant victory

5.meaning: An adjective meaning 'clear, plain, manifest' — describing something that is obvious and self-evident, or that makes things clear.
5.grammar: An active participle of form IV (mubīn), 'one that is manifest / makes clear.' The mu- prefix forms the participle. The final -an (tanwīn fatḥa) is the indefinite accusative ending ('a clear one'), used here to agree with a preceding masculine accusative noun it describes.

1.meaning: So that He may forgive — introducing a purpose clause expressing the divine aim of granting the victory: the forgiveness of the Prophet's shortcomings.

parts.en: so that He may forgive (lām of purpose + 3rd masc. sg. subjunctive)

1.grammar: Lām al-taʿlīl + imperfect verb in the subjunctive mood (manṣūb), 3rd person masculine singular, Form I. The -a ending marks the subjunctive triggered by the lām.
1.root: غ-ف-ر (gh-f-r) — to forgive, to cover, to pardon

2.meaning: 'For You / to You' — a 'for/to' particle attached to the pronoun 'You,' indicating that something is directed toward, or done for the sake of, a single addressee.
2.grammar: A small phrase: the particle li- ('for / to,' vowelled la- before a pronoun) joined to the attached pronoun -ka, 'you' (one masculine addressee). The pronoun is in the form used as the object of a preposition, marking the person as the one to whom or for whom the action is directed.
2.root: — (particle + pronoun, no triliteral root)

3.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
3.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.
3.root: — (proper divine name)

4.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
4.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

5.meaning: What preceded, what came before — past actions or shortcomings that occurred before a given point. Used here of sins or lapses that preceded the revelation of this verse.

parts.en: preceded / came before (3rd masc. sg. past, Form V)

5.grammar: Past tense verb (māḍī), 3rd person masculine singular, Form V (tafaʿʿala pattern), expressing going forward or preceding in time.
5.root: ق-د-م (q-d-m) — to precede, to go forward, to come before

6.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
6.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.
6.root: — (preposition)

7.meaning: Your sin, your fault — a lapse or moral failing attributed to the person addressed (masculine singular 'you'). In the Qur'anic context of 48:2, it refers to anything held against the Prophet in a metaphorical sense.
7.grammar: Masculine noun in the genitive case (majrūr) as the object of the preposition min (from), in construct (iḍāfa) with the possessive suffix -ka.
7.root: ذ-ن-ب (dh-n-b) — sin, fault, tail (metaphor: something trailing behind)

8.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
8.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.
8.root: — (relative pronoun / particle)

9.meaning: 'He delayed / lagged behind / stayed back' — to put oneself or something later, to hold back rather than going forward.
9.grammar: A past-tense form-V verb (the ta- prefix with doubled middle root gives the reflexive sense 'to put oneself behind/later'). The final -a (fatḥa) is the past-tense ending marking a single masculine subject ('he') who completed the action.
9.root: أ-خ-ر (ʾ-kh-r) — to be later, last, behind

10.meaning: And He completes / and so that He may complete — expressing divine purpose of bringing something to its full measure. Here it refers to completing the favour (niʿma) upon the Prophet.

parts.en: He completes / may complete (3rd masc. sg. subjunctive, Form IV)

10.grammar: Conjunction wāw + imperfect verb in the subjunctive mood (manṣūb), 3rd person masculine singular, Form IV (afʿala), expressing completion or perfection. The -a ending marks the subjunctive.
10.root: ت-م-م (t-m-m) — to complete, to perfect, to bring to fullness

11.meaning: A noun meaning 'His blessing / favour / bounty' — a grace or gift bestowed. 'Niʿma' is a benefaction or state of well-being granted by a giver.
11.grammar: A singular noun with the attached possessive -hu ('his'). The -a vowel before the suffix marks the accusative/object case, typically identifying the noun as the thing acted upon or received.

12.meaning: "upon you / to you / against you" — the preposition ʿalā ('on, upon, over') with the 'you' pronoun, carrying senses of resting upon, being directed to, or bearing upon someone.
12.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The base ʿalā shifts to ʿalay- when a pronoun is added. The suffix -ka means 'you' (second-person masculine singular). Prepositions themselves take no case ending.

13.meaning: And He guides you — a divine act of leading the addressed person (the Prophet) along the straight and right path. Carries the sense of continuous divine guidance.
13.grammar: Conjunction wāw + imperfect verb in the subjunctive mood, 3rd person masculine singular, Form I (yahdī → yahdiya in subjunctive), with attached 2nd person masculine singular object pronoun.
13.root: ه-د-ي (h-d-y) — to guide, to show the way, to direct

14.meaning: 'A path', 'a way', 'a road' — a clear route or way that one travels, often used for a course of conduct or a way of life.
14.grammar: A noun. The '-an' ending is the indefinite accusative with nunation ('a path', not 'the path'); the accusative typically marks the direct object of a verb.

15.meaning: 'Straight', 'upright', 'level' — describes something direct and without crookedness or deviation; figuratively, correct and sound.
15.grammar: An active participle (a 'doer'-form describing a state) on the 'mustafʿil' pattern, literally 'that which holds itself straight'. The '-an' ending is the indefinite accusative with nunation, agreeing with the indefinite accusative noun it describes.
15.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — standing, being upright; here, being straight

1.meaning: And He helps you / and so that Allah may help you — expressing divine assistance and support. The wāw connects it to the preceding purpose clause.

parts.en: He helps / may help (3rd masc. sg. subjunctive)

1.grammar: Conjunction wāw + imperfect verb in the subjunctive mood, 3rd person masculine singular, Form I (naṣara), with attached 2nd person masculine singular object pronoun. The -a ending marks subjunctive.
1.root: ن-ص-ر (n-ṣ-r) — to help, to support, to grant victory

2.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
2.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.
2.root: — (proper divine name)

3.meaning: 'Help, assistance, victory' — a noun naming the act of aiding someone against an adversary or granting them triumph. The -an ending presents it as an indefinite 'some help / any help.'
3.grammar: A noun in the indefinite accusative: the -an ending (written with a final alif) typically marks the word as a direct object of a verb, or as 'some/any (help)' without 'the.'
3.root: ن-ص-ر (n-ṣ-r) — to help, aid, give victory

4.meaning: Mighty, all-powerful, invincible — one who is dominant and cannot be overcome; also carrying the sense of precious and held in high honor. Of a person it means strong and unassailable.
4.grammar: An intensive adjective (of the faʿīl pattern, conveying a deep, settled quality). The final -an (tanwīn fatḥ) marks it as indefinite and in the accusative case, which typically signals a direct object or a descriptive complement governed into the accusative.
4.root: ع-ز-ز (ʿ-z-z) — might, strength, dominance; also honor and preciousness

1.meaning: 'He' — the standalone (independent) pronoun for a single masculine person or thing, used for emphasis or to stand as the subject on its own.
1.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, third-person masculine singular. It does not take case endings; its fixed final -a is part of the word. It serves to name or emphasize the subject ('He is the one who…').

2.meaning: A relative pronoun meaning 'the one who' or 'which' — it points back to a masculine singular person or thing and introduces a clause that describes or identifies it. It works like the English 'who/which/that' that opens a defining clause.
2.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) masculine singular relative pronoun: its form does not change for case, so the ending stays -ī whatever grammatical role it fills. It always needs a following clause to complete its meaning.

3.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'he sent down, he caused to descend, he revealed' — used especially of Allah sending down revelation, rain, or blessings from above.
3.grammar: A completed (past) action by a single masculine subject ('he'); the -a ending marks third-person masculine singular. The form IV (causative) pattern means 'to make something come down,' i.e., to send it down.
3.root: ن-ز-ل (n-z-l) — coming down, descending, alighting

4.meaning: The tranquility, the peace of heart — a special inner calm and reassurance sent by Allah upon the believers' hearts in times of fear or stress. A spiritual state of steadfast serenity.

parts.en: the tranquility / the peace of heart (definite accusative)

4.grammar: Definite feminine noun with the definite article al-, in the accusative case (manṣūb) marked by the -a ending (fatḥa). Serves as the direct object of the verb anzala (He sent down).
4.root: س-ك-ن (s-k-n) — to dwell, to be still, to find peace; sakinah = divine tranquility

5.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
5.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

6.meaning: Hearts — the inner organ understood as the seat of feeling, intention, understanding, and faith. 'Qulūb' is the plural of 'qalb' (heart).
6.grammar: A plural noun ('hearts') with the -i ending, the genitive case — which typically links it to a preceding noun ('… of the hearts') or follows a preposition ('in the hearts').
6.root: ق-ل-ب (q-l-b) — to turn over; the heart, that which fluctuates and turns

7.meaning: A plural noun meaning 'the believers' — those who have faith, who inwardly trust and affirm. The Form IV participle denotes one who brings about belief and security within.
7.grammar: A definite plural active participle of Form IV (āmana 'to believe'). The -īna ending marks a sound masculine plural in the accusative/genitive (object or oblique) state. The prefixed mu- marks it as a Form IV participle ('one who has/gives faith').
7.root: ء-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — faith, safety, security

8.meaning: A verb phrase meaning 'so that they may increase' or 'in order that they grow more' — to gain more of something, to add to one's store; from a root meaning increase or surplus.

parts.en: increase / grow more (Form VIII verb stem)

8.grammar: A present/future-tense Form VIII (iftaʿala) verb, 'to increase oneself, to grow more'. It is governed by the prefixed 'li-' ('so that, in order that'), which puts the verb in the subjunctive — hence the dropped final 'n' (it would be 'yazdādūna' as a plain statement). The 'ya-' prefix and '-ū' ending mark a third-person masculine plural subject.
8.root: ز-ي-د (z-y-d) — increase, addition, surplus, growth

9.meaning: Faith — a deep, trusting belief and inner security of heart; to affirm and entrust oneself to the truth. More than intellectual assent, it conveys trust, fidelity, and the safety that comes from believing.
9.grammar: A verbal noun (Form IV, conveying 'to bring about security/belief'). The -an ending is the indefinite accusative ('tanwīn'): it commonly marks an indefinite object of a verb or specifies in what respect something occurs ('in respect of faith').
9.root: ء-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — security, safety, trust; freedom from fear and the faith built upon it.

10.meaning: With; in the company of, alongside, together with — expressing accompaniment or togetherness.
10.grammar: An adverb of accompaniment that behaves like a preposition ('with / along with'). It is followed by a noun in the genitive case and itself typically carries the '-a' ending. It conveys being together in place, time, or company.

11.meaning: 'Their belief / their faith.' 'Īmān' is faith — a firm, trusting inner assent and security of heart in what is true, expressed in word and deed. Combined here with 'their.'
11.grammar: A verbal noun (from 'āmana,' to believe) with the attached possessive -him ('their,' masculine plural). The -i vowel on 'īmān' is the genitive case (after a preposition or in a possessive link); the -i form of the suffix (-him) follows that 'i' sound.

12.meaning: A phrase meaning 'and to Allah (belongs)' — expressing ownership or rightful belonging to Allah; the lām conveys possession or entitlement.
12.grammar: The conjunction 'wa-' ('and') joined to the prepositional phrase 'lillāhi'. This phrase is the preposition 'li-' ('to/for', here showing possession) prefixed to the name 'Allah'; when 'li-' attaches, the connecting hamza and the first lām of the definite article are elided in writing, leaving a single written lām for the preposition followed by the doubled (shadda-bearing) lām of the name. 'Allah' takes the -i (genitive) ending required after a preposition.

13.meaning: Hosts, armies, forces — plural of jund (soldier/army). Refers to the unseen divine armies or the forces Allah deploys in support of the believers.
13.grammar: Broken plural of jund (جُنْد), in the nominative case (marfūʿ) as subject or predicate.
13.root: ج-ن-د (j-n-d) — soldier, army, host; junūd = armies

14.meaning: The heavens / the skies — the plural of 'heaven', referring to the skies above and the celestial realms; the elevated expanse over the earth.
14.grammar: A definite feminine plural noun with the prefix 'al-' ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the heavens') or follows a preposition. In the sound feminine plural, this -i form also covers what would be an object role.

15.meaning: 'And the earth' — the connective 'and' joined to 'the earth', meaning the ground, land, or the world beneath the sky.
15.grammar: The connective 'wa-' ('and') with the definite feminine noun 'al-arḍ' ('the earth'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the earth') or follows a preposition, here matching the case of what it is joined to.

16.meaning: And he was / he became — a verb of being that places a subject in a past state or links it to a description in the past.
16.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'kāna' is a past-tense verb, 3rd-person masculine singular, meaning 'he was/became'; it commonly introduces a past condition and is typically followed by a noun describing the subject's state. The final -a marks completed past action by a single male.

17.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
17.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

18.meaning: All-Knowing; one possessing complete, perfect knowledge. As an intensive form it conveys knowledge that is total and unfailing, encompassing all things.
18.grammar: An intensive adjective ('all-knowing') on the faʿīl pattern, which stresses the quality to its fullest degree. The -an (tanwīn) joins the -a accusative ending — typical of a predicate or object — with the -n marking it indefinite.

19.meaning: All-Wise; one possessing perfect wisdom, who places everything in its right place and decides with flawless judgement. As an intensive form it conveys wisdom that is complete and sound.
19.grammar: An intensive adjective ('all-wise') on the faʿīl pattern, stressing the quality to its fullest degree. The -an (tanwīn) combines the -a accusative ending — typical of a predicate or object — with the -n marking it indefinite.

1.meaning: So that He may admit — expressing purpose: Allah's aim of entering/admitting a group (believers) into a specified place (Gardens of Paradise). Lām of purpose + subjunctive.

parts.en: He may admit / cause to enter (Form IV subjunctive)

1.grammar: Lām al-taʿlīl + imperfect verb in the subjunctive mood, 3rd person masculine singular, Form IV (adkhala → yudkhilu → yudkhila in subjunctive). Expresses causing entry.
1.root: د-خ-ل (d-kh-l) — to enter; Form IV: to admit, to cause to enter

2.meaning: A plural noun meaning 'the believers' — those who have faith, who inwardly trust and affirm. The Form IV participle denotes one who brings about belief and security within.
2.grammar: A definite plural active participle of Form IV (āmana 'to believe'). The -īna ending marks a sound masculine plural in the accusative/genitive (object or oblique) state. The prefixed mu- marks it as a Form IV participle ('one who has/gives faith').
2.root: ء-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — faith, safety, security

3.meaning: And the believing women — the feminine plural of those who have faith, who place their trust and security in Allah and inwardly affirm the truth.
3.grammar: An active participle (one who believes) in the sound feminine plural. The prefix wa- means 'and'; al- is the definite article 'the'. The ending -āti is the sound feminine plural marker in its genitive or accusative form (the -i vowel rather than -u): it names a group of females and signals that the word is governed by a preceding preposition, oath, or verb, or is linked to a following noun.
3.root: ء-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — to be secure, to trust, to have faith

4.meaning: 'Gardens' — the plural of a lush, walled garden thick with trees whose foliage covers the ground. The root sense is concealment by dense greenery; it is the standard word for the gardens of Paradise.
4.grammar: An indefinite sound feminine plural noun ('gardens'). The '-in' (tanwīn) ending marks it as indefinite ('some gardens'), and for this plural form it stands in the oblique case (genitive or accusative), used after prepositions/possessives or as a direct object.
4.root: ج-ن-ن (j-n-n) — to cover, conceal, hide (hence a dense garden)

5.meaning: A verb 'it flows, runs, streams' — used of water and rivers moving along, and of things that run or course freely. It describes continuous, ongoing motion.
5.grammar: A present/imperfect verb, 3rd person feminine singular. The ta- prefix here marks a feminine 'it/she' subject. The verb describes an ongoing or habitual action: 'it flows / keeps flowing.'

6.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
6.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.
6.root: — (preposition)

7.meaning: 'Beneath it / underneath it' — the noun for the underside or lower region of something, with an attached pronoun 'its' (referring to a feminine thing). It points to the space below or underneath a thing.
7.grammar: A location noun ('underneath') with the attached pronoun '-hā' ('its/her'), referring to a feminine noun. The -i ending is the genitive case, normally triggered here because words of place like 'under' commonly follow a preposition such as 'from' (min taḥti = 'from beneath').
7.root: ت-ح-ت (t-ḥ-t) — underneath, below

8.meaning: 'The rivers / the streams' — the definite plural of a word for a flowing river or watercourse. It denotes large, running channels of water.
8.grammar: A definite plural noun ('the rivers'). The -u ending is the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence — the doer of the verb or the thing being described.
8.root: ن-ه-ر (n-h-r) — river, flowing water

9.meaning: Ones who abide / remain forever — those who dwell perpetually and permanently in a state or place, without end. The word denotes lasting, undying permanence.
9.grammar: An active participle (a 'doer' word: 'ones abiding'). The -īna ending is the sound masculine plural in its accusative/genitive form, used when the word is an object or governed by a preceding element. It describes people characterized by perpetual abiding.
9.root: خ-ل-د (kh-l-d) — perpetuity, everlasting abiding

10.meaning: 'In it / therein.' A preposition with an attached pronoun: 'in' plus a feminine singular 'it,' meaning 'inside it / within it,' referring back to some feminine or grammatically feminine thing (such as a place).
10.grammar: A prepositional phrase: fī ('in, within') with the attached object pronoun -hā ('it,' feminine singular). The pronoun is the object of the preposition and points back to a previously mentioned feminine noun.

11.meaning: And He removes / so that He may remove — referring to the removal of sins or evil deeds, the covering and expiation of moral failings.

parts.en: He removes / expiate (3rd masc. sg. subjunctive, Form II)

11.grammar: Conjunction wāw + imperfect verb in subjunctive mood, 3rd person masculine singular, Form II (kaffara → yukaffiru → yukaffira). -a ending marks subjunctive.
11.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover; Form II: to expiate, to atone for, to remove (sins)

12.meaning: From them; away from them; concerning them. The preposition ʿan conveys moving away from, departing from, or 'on behalf of / concerning', combined with the pronoun 'them'.
12.grammar: A preposition joined to the attached pronoun -hum, 'them' (referring to a group, grammatically masculine plural). The preposition ʿan basically signals separation or removal ('away from'), and can also mean 'about/concerning' or 'on behalf of' depending on usage.

13.meaning: Their evil deeds, misdeeds, or wrongs — bad actions and the harm or offence they carry; with the attached pronoun, the misdeeds belonging to them.
13.grammar: A feminine sound plural noun (singular sayyiʾa) with the attached possessive 'their'. The -i vowel before -him reflects the genitive/possessive linkage to that pronoun.

14.meaning: And he was / he became — a verb of being that places a subject in a past state or links it to a description in the past.
14.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'kāna' is a past-tense verb, 3rd-person masculine singular, meaning 'he was/became'; it commonly introduces a past condition and is typically followed by a noun describing the subject's state. The final -a marks completed past action by a single male.

15.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that' — pointing to something regarded as distant or elevated, as opposed to 'this' (hadha) for what is near. It singles out a masculine singular thing and lends it a sense of distinction or loftiness.
15.grammar: A demonstrative for a masculine singular referent at a distance. The -ka ending is an address particle directed at a single male listener; it does not change for case. The whole word stays fixed in form regardless of its grammatical position.

16.meaning: 'With / in the presence of / near' — an adverb of place and relation meaning at, by, in the sight or estimation of someone. It indicates nearness, possession, or what holds in someone's view (as in 'with Allah' = in His sight).
16.grammar: An adverb of place that is always followed by a noun it relates to. It carries a fixed -a ending; this accusative-type vowel is characteristic of such adverbs of place and shows the word is functioning to locate something ('at, near, in the presence of').

17.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
17.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

18.meaning: A noun meaning 'triumph, great success, winning, salvation' — a decisive attainment of what is sought together with deliverance from what is feared. It denotes the highest kind of winning, not merely a minor gain.
18.grammar: An indefinite masculine verbal noun. The '-an' ending (nunation with a final 'alif') marks it as indefinite ('a triumph') and as accusative — the case typically used for the object of a verb, or for a noun that specifies or reinforces an action (as in 'he triumphed a triumph,' i.e. 'a real triumph').

19.meaning: 'Great, immense, mighty, momentous.' It describes something vast in size, weight, or seriousness, and is often used of grave or awe-inspiring matters.
19.grammar: An adjective on the intensive faʿīl pattern. The -an ending is the indefinite accusative ('a great …'), commonly marking an adjective that agrees with an indefinite accusative noun it describes, or the object of a verb.

1.meaning: And He may punish — referring to divine punishment of hypocrite men; part of a purpose clause indicating what Allah will do to those who associate partners with Him.

parts.en: He may punish (3rd masc. sg. subjunctive, Form II)

1.grammar: Conjunction wāw + imperfect verb in subjunctive mood, 3rd person masculine singular, Form II (ʿadhdhaba). -a ending marks subjunctive.
1.root: ع-ذ-ب (ʿ-dh-b) — to punish, to cause to suffer; ʿadhāb = punishment

2.meaning: the hypocrites — those who outwardly profess faith while inwardly concealing disbelief; people who present one face publicly and hide another within. From a root evoking a tunnel with two openings, suggesting a hidden way out.
2.grammar: A definite noun: al- means 'the'. 'Munāfiq' is an active participle of Form III ('one who behaves hypocritically'). The ending -īna marks the masculine sound plural in the oblique case (the form used for objects of verbs and after prepositions, i.e. accusative/genitive, as opposed to nominative -ūna).
2.root: ن-ف-ق (n-f-q) — tunnel/burrow with a hidden exit; hence hypocrisy

3.meaning: 'And the hypocrites (women)' — the feminine plural counterpart of the male hypocrites: women who outwardly profess faith while concealing disbelief. The leading 'and' joins them to what precedes; this is the definite feminine plural in the object/oblique form.
3.grammar: A definite sound feminine plural noun, with wa- ('and') and al- ('the') prefixed. The -āt is the feminine plural marker, and the final -i is the accusative/genitive case — the form used for a direct object, after a preposition, or linked to a preceding noun. (In a sound feminine plural this same -i serves both the object and the genitive, contrasting with -u for the subject.)
3.root: ن-ف-ق (n-f-q) — a tunnel with two exits; hence hypocrisy (a hidden second way out)

4.meaning: And the polytheist men — those men who associate partners with Allah. The conjunction wāw links this group to the preceding munāfiqīn (hypocrites) as an additional object of divine punishment.

parts.en: the polytheist men / those who associate partners (masculine plural accusative)

4.grammar: Conjunction wāw + definite masculine sound plural noun in the accusative case (manṣūb), marked by the /-īna/ ending.
4.root: ش-ر-ك (sh-r-k) — to share, to associate; mush'rik = one who associates partners with Allah

5.meaning: And the polytheist women — the female counterpart to the previous entry; women who associate partners with Allah, listed alongside polytheist men as objects of divine punishment.
5.grammar: Conjunction wāw + definite feminine sound plural noun, marked by the /-āti/ ending. In the accusative case as the second object.
5.root: ش-ر-ك (sh-r-k) — to associate partners; mush'rikāt = polytheist women

6.meaning: Those who entertain evil assumptions / those who think ill — people who harbor a negative opinion or false suspicion about Allah. Refers to hypocrites and polytheists who doubted Allah's support for the Prophet.

parts.en: those who think (evil) / those who assume wrongly (masculine plural accusative)

6.grammar: Definite active participle, masculine sound plural in the accusative case, Form I (ẓanna — to think/assume). Marked by /-īna/.
6.root: ظ-ن-ن (ẓ-n-n) — to think, to assume; often carries connotation of suspicion or false assumption

7.meaning: A phrase 'in Allah / by Allah', combining the preposition 'with/in/by' and the divine name Allah, the proper name of the One God.
7.grammar: The preposition bi- ('in, with, by means of') prefixed to the divine name Allah. A preposition always forces the following noun into the genitive case, which is why Allah here ends in -i. With verbs of believing, bi- conveys the object of faith — to believe IN.
7.root: — (Allah is the proper name of God and is not derived from a triliteral root in the usual sense)

8.meaning: Conjecture, supposition, opinion, or assumption — a thought held with less than certainty. Depending on context it ranges from reasonable supposition to baseless guesswork; here it is the noun "thinking/assumption."
8.grammar: A noun with the -a ending, which is accusative. This ending typically marks the noun as the direct object of a verb, or as the first term in a tightly-bound "… of …" possessive phrase when it leads into a following genitive noun.
8.root: ظ-ن-ن (ẓ-n-n) — to suppose, conjecture, think; holding an opinion short of certainty

9.meaning: 'The evil, the bad, the harmful' — that which is wicked, woeful, or calamitous; misfortune and ill. As a noun it denotes badness or harm in general.
9.grammar: A noun made definite by al- ('the'). The final -i is the genitive case: it typically links the word to a preceding noun ('the … OF evil') or follows a preposition. Here the genitive marks it as the second term of a possessive phrase ('the … of evil').
9.root: س-و-ء (s-w-ʾ) — to be bad/evil; harm, misfortune

10.meaning: A compound meaning 'upon them' or 'against them': the preposition ʿalā ('on, upon, over, against') joined to the plural pronoun 'them'. It conveys something resting on, being incumbent upon, or weighing against a group.
10.grammar: ʿalā shifts to the form ʿalay- before a pronoun. The suffix -him is the attached pronominal suffix for a masculine plural group ('them'); after a preposition it carries genitive/prepositional force, and the -i- vowel reflects its position after this preposition. Together they signal a relationship of something being over, upon, or burdensome to that group.
10.root: — (preposition with attached pronoun; no triliteral root)

11.meaning: 'A turn (of fortune), a circling event, a reversal' — a single instance of fate coming round upon someone; a turn of misfortune (or, by context, of good or ill) that encircles a person.
11.grammar: A feminine singular noun (active participle in form, 'that which circles'), marked feminine by the -at- ending. The final -u is the nominative case, the form used for a subject or predicate ('a turn [of fortune is] …'). The bare ending (without nunation) also signals that it stands in a possessive link with a following noun ('the turn OF …').

12.meaning: 'The evil, the bad, the harmful' — that which is wicked, woeful, or calamitous; misfortune and ill. As a noun it denotes badness or harm in general.
12.grammar: A noun made definite by al- ('the'). The final -i is the genitive case: it typically links the word to a preceding noun ('the … OF evil') or follows a preposition. Here the genitive marks it as the second term of a possessive phrase ('the … of evil').
12.root: س-و-ء (s-w-ʾ) — to be bad/evil; harm, misfortune

13.meaning: 'And He grew angry / was wrathful' — a perfect verb expressing anger and displeasure, here joined by 'and'.
13.grammar: The conjunction wa- ('and') plus a perfect verb, 3rd-person masculine singular. With no prefix and the final -a, it states a completed act, 'he became angry'.

14.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
14.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

15.meaning: A compound meaning 'upon them' or 'against them': the preposition ʿalā ('on, upon, over, against') joined to the plural pronoun 'them'. It conveys something resting on, being incumbent upon, or weighing against a group.
15.grammar: ʿalā shifts to the form ʿalay- before a pronoun. The suffix -him is the attached pronominal suffix for a masculine plural group ('them'); after a preposition it carries genitive/prepositional force, and the -i- vowel reflects its position after this preposition. Together they signal a relationship of something being over, upon, or burdensome to that group.
15.root: — (preposition with attached pronoun; no triliteral root)

16.meaning: And He has cursed them — Allah's curse upon those who associate partners with Him: His rejection and removal of His mercy from them.
16.grammar: Conjunction wāw + past tense verb (māḍī), 3rd person masculine singular + attached 3rd person masculine plural object pronoun.
16.root: ل-ع-ن (l-ʿ-n) — to curse, to expel from mercy

17.meaning: 'And He prepared / made ready' — a perfect verb meaning to ready, arrange, or set in store something in advance; here joined by 'and'.
17.grammar: The conjunction wa- ('and') plus a perfect verb (form IV), 3rd-person masculine singular. It states a completed act, 'he prepared'; the doubled final consonant reflects this form's pattern.

18.meaning: 'To them' or 'for them' — directing something toward, or assigning it to, a group of males (or a mixed group).
18.grammar: The preposition li- ('to / for'), here voweled 'la-', joined to the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The preposition expresses direction, recipient, or possession ('to / for'), and -hum identifies a third-person masculine plural object, 'them'.

19.meaning: Jahannam — a proper name for the Fire of punishment in the Hereafter, the abode of torment. It is a name rather than a descriptive common noun.
19.grammar: A proper name. Because it is a special, non-fully-inflecting noun (it does not take tanwīn), it shows the -a ending in places where most nouns would otherwise take -i; here the single -a serves for both accusative and genitive positions. As a name it carries no general dictionary 'meaning' but designates the abode of punishment.
19.root: — (a proper name; commonly treated as having no Arabic triliteral root)

20.meaning: 'And it became evil / how evil it is' — a past-tense verb of dispraise expressing that something is bad, wretched, or a wicked outcome. Used to condemn a thing as an evil example.
20.grammar: A third-person feminine singular past-tense verb ('it/she was evil'). The -at ending marks a feminine subject. As a verb of blame it functions like an exclamation of dispraise ('how evil … is!'). The wa- prefix means 'and.'
20.root: س-و-ء (s-w-ʾ) — evil, badness, to be bad/wretched

21.meaning: 'A destination / journey's end / final outcome' — the place or state to which something ultimately comes or returns. It denotes where one ends up.
21.grammar: A noun of place/outcome on the maC-īC pattern, derived from a hollow root, ending in a sound consonant (rāʾ). The tanwīn fatḥ (-an) sits on that final consonant and marks the noun as indefinite and accusative — the case used for an object or for a noun specifying respect ('… as a destination').
21.root: ص-ي-ر (ṣ-y-r) — to come to, to end up, to become; an outcome/destination

1.meaning: A phrase meaning 'and to Allah (belongs)' — expressing ownership or rightful belonging to Allah; the lām conveys possession or entitlement.
1.grammar: The conjunction 'wa-' ('and') joined to the prepositional phrase 'lillāhi'. This phrase is the preposition 'li-' ('to/for', here showing possession) prefixed to the name 'Allah'; when 'li-' attaches, the connecting hamza and the first lām of the definite article are elided in writing, leaving a single written lām for the preposition followed by the doubled (shadda-bearing) lām of the name. 'Allah' takes the -i (genitive) ending required after a preposition.

2.meaning: Hosts, armies, forces — plural of jund (soldier/army). Refers to the unseen divine armies or the forces Allah deploys in support of the believers.
2.grammar: Broken plural of jund (جُنْد), in the nominative case (marfūʿ) as subject or predicate.
2.root: ج-ن-د (j-n-d) — soldier, army, host; junūd = armies

3.meaning: The heavens / the skies — the plural of 'heaven', referring to the skies above and the celestial realms; the elevated expanse over the earth.
3.grammar: A definite feminine plural noun with the prefix 'al-' ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the heavens') or follows a preposition. In the sound feminine plural, this -i form also covers what would be an object role.
3.root: س-م-و (s-m-w) — height, sky

4.meaning: 'And the earth' — the connective 'and' joined to 'the earth', meaning the ground, land, or the world beneath the sky.
4.grammar: The connective 'wa-' ('and') with the definite feminine noun 'al-arḍ' ('the earth'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the earth') or follows a preposition, here matching the case of what it is joined to.
4.root: أ-ر-ض (ʾ-r-ḍ) — earth, land

5.meaning: And he was / he became — a verb of being that places a subject in a past state or links it to a description in the past.
5.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'kāna' is a past-tense verb, 3rd-person masculine singular, meaning 'he was/became'; it commonly introduces a past condition and is typically followed by a noun describing the subject's state. The final -a marks completed past action by a single male.

6.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
6.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.
6.root: — (proper divine name)

7.meaning: Mighty, all-powerful, invincible — one who is dominant and cannot be overcome; also carrying the sense of precious and held in high honor. Of a person it means strong and unassailable.
7.grammar: An intensive adjective (of the faʿīl pattern, conveying a deep, settled quality). The final -an (tanwīn fatḥ) marks it as indefinite and in the accusative case, which typically signals a direct object or a descriptive complement governed into the accusative.
7.root: ع-ز-ز (ʿ-z-z) — might, strength, dominance; also honor and preciousness

8.meaning: All-Wise; one possessing perfect wisdom, who places everything in its right place and decides with flawless judgement. As an intensive form it conveys wisdom that is complete and sound.
8.grammar: An intensive adjective ('all-wise') on the faʿīl pattern, stressing the quality to its fullest degree. The -an (tanwīn) combines the -a accusative ending — typical of a predicate or object — with the -n marking it indefinite.
8.root: ح-ك-م (ḥ-k-m) — wisdom, sound judgement, governance

1.meaning: A two-part expression: an emphatic particle that strongly affirms and confirms a statement ('truly, indeed, certainly'), fused with the attached pronoun 'we.' Together: 'truly we…' / 'indeed we…'
1.grammar: The particle inna gives strong emphasis and certainty to the clause it opens. The attached -ā is the pronoun 'we,' serving as the subject being emphasized: 'truly we…'

2.meaning: 'We sent you / We dispatched you' — the act of sending forth one male addressee, as one is sent on a mission or as a messenger.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb on the form-IV ('afʿala') pattern (to send), with two attached pronouns: 'nā' is the subject 'we,' and the final 'ka' is the object 'you' (one male). So it states a completed act, 'we sent you.'
2.root: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — to send; a messenger/envoy

3.meaning: A witness — one who bears testimony, who is present and testifies to what he has seen. As a Qur'anic epithet of the Prophet, it means he witnesses his community's deeds and testifies on their behalf or against them on the Day of Judgment.
3.grammar: Indefinite active participle (Form I), masculine singular in the accusative case (manṣūb), marked by tanwīn fatḥ (-an). Functions as a ḥāl (circumstantial complement) or predicate.
3.root: ش-ه-د (sh-h-d) — to witness, to testify, to be present; shāhid = witness

4.meaning: And a bearer of glad tidings — one who brings good news, an announcer of good things to come. One of the Prophet's titles: he brings the glad tidings of Allah's mercy and Paradise to the believers.

parts.en: a bearer of glad tidings (indefinite masculine accusative)

4.grammar: Conjunction wāw + indefinite active participle Form II (bashshara → mubashshir), masculine singular in the accusative case, marked by tanwīn fatḥ (-an).
4.root: ب-ش-ر (b-sh-r) — to bring good news; Form II: to announce glad tidings; mubashshir = one who brings good news

5.meaning: One who warns; a herald who cautions of impending danger or consequence, urging heedfulness.
5.grammar: The prefix wa- means 'and', joining this to what precedes. The stem is an intensive/agent noun on the faʿīl pattern, naming one who warns. The final -an (accusative with nunation) marks it indefinite and typically signals an object or a state/role ('as a …').
5.root: ن-ذ-ر (n-dh-r) — to warn, caution; a solemn vow/pledge

1.meaning: So that you (plural) may believe — expressing purpose: the reason for sending the Prophet as witness and announcer was so that the community would believe in Allah and His Messenger.

parts.en: you (pl.) may believe (2nd masc. pl. subjunctive)

1.grammar: Lām al-taʿlīl + imperfect verb in the subjunctive mood, 2nd person masculine plural, Form IV (āmana). The wāw is dropped before the subjunctive alif.
1.root: أ-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — to be safe, to trust; Form IV: to believe, to have faith

2.meaning: A phrase 'in Allah / by Allah', combining the preposition 'with/in/by' and the divine name Allah, the proper name of the One God.
2.grammar: The preposition bi- ('in, with, by means of') prefixed to the divine name Allah. A preposition always forces the following noun into the genitive case, which is why Allah here ends in -i. With verbs of believing, bi- conveys the object of faith — to believe IN.
2.root: — (Allah is the proper name of God and is not derived from a triliteral root in the usual sense)

3.meaning: A phrase meaning 'and His Messenger' — referring to one who is sent, an envoy or apostle bearing a message, joined by 'and' and possessed by 'His.'
3.grammar: 'Messenger' joined by wa- ('and') and followed by the possessive pronoun -hi ('his'). The -i vowel before the pronoun is the genitive case, here because the word is linked in possession ('Messenger OF Him'); the pronoun takes the -hi form (with i-vowel) when it follows an i-sound.
3.root: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — sending, dispatching; a message or one who is sent

4.meaning: And you (plural) may honour / support him — referring to honouring and supporting the Prophet. The verb carries the sense of assisting with reverence and helping with might.

parts.en: you (pl.) honour / support (2nd masc. pl. subjunctive, Form II)

4.grammar: Conjunction wāw + imperfect verb in subjunctive mood, 2nd person masculine plural, Form II (ʿazzara), with attached 3rd person masculine singular object pronoun.
4.root: ع-ز-ر (ʿ-z-r) — to support, to help, to honour, to strengthen

5.meaning: And you (plural) may revere / respect him — to hold the Prophet in high esteem and treat him with the deep respect he deserves as the Messenger of Allah.

parts.en: you (pl.) revere / respect (2nd masc. pl. subjunctive, Form II)

5.grammar: Conjunction wāw + imperfect verb in subjunctive mood, 2nd person masculine plural, Form II (waqqara), with attached 3rd person masculine singular object pronoun.
5.root: و-ق-ر (w-q-r) — to be weighty, dignified; Form II: to revere, to respect, to venerate

6.meaning: And you (plural) may glorify Him — to glorify Allah with tasbīḥ (declaring His transcendence and perfection), morning and evening. Refers to the believers glorifying Allah alongside their service to the Prophet.

parts.en: you (pl.) glorify (2nd masc. pl. subjunctive, Form II)

6.grammar: Conjunction wāw + imperfect verb in subjunctive mood, 2nd person masculine plural, Form II (sabbaḥa → yusabbiḥu), with attached 3rd person masculine singular object pronoun.
6.root: س-ب-ح (s-b-ḥ) — to swim, to glide; Form II: to glorify Allah (tasbīḥ), to declare His transcendence

7.meaning: Morning, daybreak, the early part of the day — the time from dawn until mid-morning.

parts.en: accusative ending on feminine noun (with nunation)

7.grammar: A feminine noun (its feminine ending is the tied-tā', pronounced '-t-' before the case vowel). The '-an' accusative ending here typically marks a time expression ('in the morning'), and the nunation shows it is indefinite.
7.root: ب-ك-ر (b-k-r) — early morning, to be early

8.meaning: And in the evening — the late afternoon / evening time. Together with bukratan (in the morning), it forms a merism indicating glorifying Allah at all times, specifically at dawn and dusk.

parts.en: in the evening / at eventide (indefinite accusative of time)

8.grammar: Indefinite masculine noun in the accusative case as an adverb of time (ẓarf al-zamān). Tanwīn fatḥ (-an) marks indefinite accusative.
8.root: أ-ص-ل (ʾ-ṣ-l) — origin, root; aṣīl = late afternoon / evening (the time when things return to their origin)

1.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
1.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: They pledge allegiance to you — they give their hand (bayʿa) to you, entering into a formal covenant of loyalty, obedience, and support. Refers to the Companions swearing allegiance to the Prophet under the tree at Hudaybiyyah (Bayʿat al-Riḍwān).

parts.en: they pledge allegiance (3rd masc. pl. present, Form III)

3.grammar: Imperfect verb, indicative mood, 3rd person masculine plural, Form III (bāyaʿa — reciprocal pledging), with attached 2nd person masculine singular object pronoun. Marked by /-ūna/ suffix.
3.root: ب-ي-ع (b-y-ʿ) — to sell, to exchange; Form III: to pledge allegiance (bayʿa = the pledge/transaction of loyalty)

4.meaning: 'Only / nothing but' — a restrictive particle that limits and emphasizes, asserting that the matter is exclusively so and no other ('it is only...'). It combines the emphatic 'inna' with the restricting 'mā'.
4.grammar: A compound particle formed from the emphatic inna ('indeed') and mā, which together work as a tool of restriction meaning 'only / nothing but'. It both stresses and confines the statement that follows to a single truth, excluding all alternatives.

5.meaning: They pledge allegiance — those who give their pledge of allegiance (to the Prophet), here expressing that in doing so they are pledging to Allah Himself.

parts.en: they pledge allegiance (3rd masc. pl. present, Form III)

5.grammar: Imperfect verb, indicative mood, 3rd person masculine plural, Form III (bāyaʿa). Marked by /-ūna/.
5.root: ب-ي-ع (b-y-ʿ) — to sell, to exchange; Form III: to pledge allegiance

6.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
6.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.
6.root: — (proper name)

7.meaning: Hand — the noun for a hand. In Arabic it commonly extends by metaphor to power, agency, generosity, or what a person does and gives.
7.grammar: A singular noun. The final -u (ḍamma) is the nominative case, the form a noun takes when it is the subject of a sentence or the thing being described; it can also be the first term of a possessive phrase ('the hand OF …').
7.root: ي-د-ي (y-d-y) — hand

8.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
8.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

9.meaning: 'Above / over / on top of.' An adverb of place meaning the higher position relative to something else; it can also mean 'superior to' or 'beyond.'
9.grammar: An adverb of place that is normally attached to a following noun ('above …'). Its fixed -a ending is the form such place-words take when they govern the noun that follows them.
9.root: ف-و-ق (f-w-q) — to be above, surpass, exceed

10.meaning: Their hands. The plural noun 'hands' carrying the masculine plural possessive 'their'; often used idiomatically for what people do, produce, or are responsible for through their own deeds.
10.grammar: A plural noun with an attached possessive pronoun '-him' meaning 'their' (a group of males, or mixed). 'aydī' is the irregular ('broken') plural of 'yad' (hand). The pronoun ending makes the whole construction definite and possessed; the 'i'-coloured stem before the suffix reflects its genitive/possessed state, the form typically following a preposition or standing as object.

11.meaning: A compound meaning 'then whoever' or 'so whoever'. It combines 'then/so' with the conditional/relative 'who', introducing whatever person meets a stated condition.
11.grammar: The connector fa- ('then/so', often answering or following a condition) joined to man ('whoever / the one who'), which refers to people and introduces a condition: 'whoever does X…'. man does not change its ending; the clause after it supplies the rest of the meaning.

12.meaning: He breaks (his oath / pledge) — referring to one who violates and breaks a covenant or pledge that he has made. Used to describe those who would betray the oath of allegiance.

parts.en: he broke (his oath) / violated (3rd masc. sg. past, Form I)

12.grammar: Past tense verb (māḍī), 3rd person masculine singular, Form I. A doubled final root (ن-ك-ث).
12.root: ن-ك-ث (n-k-th) — to unravel, to break (a pledge or rope), to renege on a covenant

13.meaning: A compound particle 'so it is only …' or 'then indeed only.' It joins a consequence ('so/then') to an emphatic restriction ('only / nothing more than'), confining the statement to exactly what follows.
13.grammar: A cluster of particles: 'fa-' introduces a result ('so/then'), 'inna' gives emphasis ('truly'), and the attached 'mā' turns the emphasis into restriction, so the whole means 'so it is only/nothing but.' These are connective and emphatic words; they have no case ending of their own.

14.meaning: He breaks / violates — the imperfect (present/future) form: one who breaks or violates a pledge. Indicates ongoing or future breach of the covenant.

parts.en: he breaks / violates (3rd masc. sg. imperfect, indicative)

14.grammar: Imperfect verb, indicative mood, 3rd person masculine singular, Form I. Marked by /-u/ (ḍamma) ending.
14.root: ن-ك-ث (n-k-th) — to unravel, to break a promise

15.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
15.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

16.meaning: 'Himself; his own self/soul' — the inner self, soul, or person of a male individual; used reflexively to point back to the person himself.
16.grammar: The noun 'nafs' ('self/soul') with the attached pronoun '-hi' ('his'). The '-i' ending is genitive: it typically follows a preposition or links the noun possessively to what precedes ('the self OF him' = 'himself'). The pronoun appears as '-hi' (rather than '-hu') because of this preceding '-i' vowel; the long vowel mark indicates it is pronounced '-hī'.

17.meaning: And whoever / and the one who — a joining word plus a relative pronoun introducing a person (or persons) defined by whatever they do; often sets up a condition ('whoever does X …').
17.grammar: A particle 'and' joined to the relative/conditional pronoun man ('whoever, who'). Man does not change its ending; it refers to people and frequently functions as a conditional, so the verb that follows it typically takes the shortened jussive mood.

18.meaning: A verb meaning 'he fulfilled / he keeps faithfully' — to discharge a commitment or keep a promise completely and faithfully. Here it describes one who fulfills his covenant in full.
18.grammar: A perfect-form (past) verb of the form-IV pattern (af'ala), 3rd-person masculine singular ('he'), built from the root for fulfilling. The initial a- is the form-IV prefix and the final long -ā is the root's weak letter, written as alif maqṣūra. Though the af'al pattern looks identical to an elative ('more/most ___') adjective, here it functions as a verb ('he who fulfills/keeps his pledge').
18.root: و-ف-ي (w-f-y) — to fulfill, complete, keep faithfully, render in full

19.meaning: A phrase meaning 'in/with that which' or 'in what' — combining the sense of 'by means of' or 'concerning' with an unspecified thing ('whatever it may be').
19.grammar: The preposition bi ('in, with, by means of, concerning') attached to the relative/indefinite pronoun mā ('what, that which'). Both elements are invariable, so the phrase carries no case ending. A word governed by the preposition bi is understood to be in the genitive relationship.

20.meaning: He has covenanted / he made a covenant — past tense, indicating that someone entered into a binding agreement or covenant with Allah. The specific covenant here is the bayʿa of allegiance.

parts.en: he covenanted / made a pact (3rd masc. sg. past, Form III)

20.grammar: Past tense verb, 3rd person masculine singular, Form III (ʿāhada — mutual pact).
20.root: ع-ه-د (ʿ-h-d) — covenant, promise; Form III: to make a covenant with someone

21.meaning: Upon him — a prepositional phrase indicating that something (the covenant) is binding on him, or that something is owed to him. The preposition ʿalā indicates obligation or location.
21.grammar: Preposition ʿalā (على) with attached 3rd person masculine singular pronoun. Takes genitive case on its object.

22.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
22.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

23.meaning: Soon He will give him — referring to the imminent divine reward: Allah will bestow upon the one who fulfils his pledge a great reward.

parts.en: He will give (3rd masc. sg. imperfect, Form IV)

23.grammar: Fa (consecutive) + sa (future particle) + imperfect verb, 3rd person masculine singular, Form IV (ātā → yu'tī), with attached 3rd person masculine singular pronoun (genitive form -hi after kasra).
23.root: أ-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come; Form IV: to give, to bestow

24.meaning: A reward, wage, or recompense — the return earned for work or conduct, whether worldly pay or otherworldly recompense.
24.grammar: A noun meaning 'a reward.' The final '-an' (tanwīn fatḥa) marks the indefinite accusative case, the case used for the object of a verb (e.g. of 'to give'), giving the sense 'a reward.'
24.root: ا-ج-ر (ʾ-j-r) — reward, wage, recompense for what one does

25.meaning: 'Great, immense, tremendous' — describing something vast in magnitude or weight, whether in size, importance, or seriousness.
25.grammar: An adjective ('great, immense') in an intensive pattern. The -an ending (nunation with a final alif) marks it as indefinite and in the accusative case — the case typically used for the object of a verb or for a description attached to such an object.
25.root: ع-ظ-م (ʿ-ẓ-m) — to be great, immense, mighty; greatness, a bone

1.meaning: 'He/it will say' — a statement of future speech. Built from the present-tense verb 'he says' with the prefixed particle sa- ('will, shall, is going to'), marking an action expected to happen soon.
1.grammar: The prefix sa- places the verb in the near future ('will say'). The base verb is present-tense, third-person masculine singular: the ya- prefix means 'he', and the final -u ending marks the indicative mood (a plain, factual statement, as opposed to commands or subjunctive forms).

2.meaning: 'For You / to You' — a 'for/to' particle attached to the pronoun 'You,' indicating that something is directed toward, or done for the sake of, a single addressee.
2.grammar: A small phrase: the particle li- ('for / to,' vowelled la- before a pronoun) joined to the attached pronoun -ka, 'you' (one masculine addressee). The pronoun is in the form used as the object of a preposition, marking the person as the one to whom or for whom the action is directed.
2.root: — (particle + pronoun, no triliteral root)

3.meaning: Those left behind / kept back: people who were caused to remain behind while others went forth, held back from joining an undertaking.

parts.en: ones left behind (passive participle, Form II, plural)

3.grammar: A passive participle ('the ones who were …') with the definite article al- ('the'). The sound masculine plural ending here is -ūna, which marks the word as the subject (the doer/topic) rather than an object. Being passive, it names a group to whom something was done — they were left behind.
3.root: خ-ل-ف (kh-l-f) — to come after, be left behind, remain in the rear

4.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
4.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

5.meaning: The bedouins; the desert-dwelling Arabs of the open country, as distinct from settled town-dwellers. A collective noun referring to nomadic Arab tribes.
5.grammar: A definite collective noun (plural pattern afʿāl) used for desert Arabs. The -i ending is genitive: it marks the word as following a preposition or linked to a preceding noun ('... of ...').

6.meaning: Our properties/wealth kept us busy — they distracted and preoccupied us. Used by the Bedouin who stayed behind as their excuse for not joining the Prophet at Hudaybiyyah.

parts.en: kept busy / distracted (3rd fem. sg. past)

6.grammar: Past tense verb, 3rd person feminine singular + attached 1st person plural object pronoun. The feminine verb agrees with the subject amwāl (properties), treated as grammatically feminine.
6.root: ش-غ-ل (sh-gh-l) — to occupy, to keep busy, to preoccupy; shughl = occupation, preoccupation

7.meaning: Our properties / our wealth — plural of māl, referring to one's possessions, livestock, and assets. Used by the stay-behinds to justify their absence.
7.grammar: Broken plural of māl (مَال), in the nominative case (marfūʿ) as the subject of the preceding verb shaghalatnā. Followed by the 1st person plural possessive suffix -nā.
7.root: م-و-ل (m-w-l) — wealth, property; amwāl = properties (plural of māl)

8.meaning: And our families / and our dependents — those under one's care and responsibility. Listed alongside amwāl (properties) as the reason given by the stay-behinds for not joining the expedition.
8.grammar: Conjunction wāw + masculine sound plural of ahl (أَهْل), in the nominative case (marfūʿ), marked by /-ūna/, with 1st person plural possessive suffix -nā (replacing final nūn).
8.root: أ-ه-ل (ʾ-h-l) — family, people, folk; ahl = family / people of a place

9.meaning: So seek forgiveness — an imperative directed at the Prophet, commanding him to ask forgiveness for (these hypocrites), ironically reinforcing that the Prophet alone could intercede for them, if he chose to.

parts.en: seek forgiveness (2nd masc. sg. imperative, Form X)

9.grammar: Consecutive fa + imperative mood, 2nd person masculine singular, Form X (istaghfara — to seek forgiveness).
9.root: غ-ف-ر (gh-f-r) — to forgive; Form X: to seek forgiveness, to ask for pardon

10.meaning: A combination of the preposition 'for / to' with the pronoun 'us', meaning 'for us' or 'to us / on our behalf'.
10.grammar: A preposition ('for / to') joined to the attached pronoun 'us'. The pronoun -nā always means 'us / our' regardless of position. Together they express benefit or direction toward the speakers ('for us').

11.meaning: 'They say / they keep saying' — a present-tense verb of speaking: to say, utter, or assert in words.
11.grammar: Present-tense verb, third-person masculine plural ('they'), from a hollow (middle-vowel) root. The ya- prefix marks the 'they/he' class, the -ū marks the masculine plural subject, and the -na ending signals the ordinary (indicative) present, 'they are saying.'

12.meaning: 'With/by their tongues' — the noun 'tongues' (the organs of speech, hence speech itself), joined to a preposition and a 'their' possessive.
12.grammar: A noun phrase opened by the preposition bi- ('with/by'). 'Alsina' is a plural noun ('tongues'). The -i ending is genitive, the case required after a preposition and before a possessive pronoun. The attached -him means 'their' for a group.

13.meaning: A short, highly versatile particle 'mā.' It can mean 'what' or 'that which,' can negate ('not'), and can serve as an intensifier attached to another word. Its precise force depends on what it accompanies, but its core is to point to a thing or to add emphasis.
13.grammar: A multifunctional particle. It does not take case endings. Depending on usage it can be a relative ('that which'), an interrogative ('what?'), a negator ('not'), or — when joined to another particle — an emphasizer. It is uninflected and indeclinable.

14.meaning: A special negating verb meaning 'is not / are not'. Unlike a simple particle, it behaves like a verb (frozen in the past-tense form) and serves to deny that something is the case, cancelling an assertion of being.
14.grammar: A defective verb fixed in the 3rd-person masculine singular ('he/it is not'). The final -a is its frozen ending; it does not conjugate for tense like other verbs. Grammatically it raises its subject to the nominative and puts its predicate in the accusative, functioning to negate a state of being.

15.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
15.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

16.meaning: 'Their hearts' — the plural of qalb ('heart'), joined to the pronoun 'their'. In Qur'anic usage the 'heart' (qalb) is the seat of understanding, intention, faith, and feeling, not merely the physical organ.
16.grammar: Qulūb is the broken (irregular) plural of qalb, 'hearts'. The -i ending is genitive: here it appears because the noun follows a preposition and because it is possessed by an attached pronoun. The suffix -him means 'their' (a masculine plural group), and its -i- vowel matches the preceding genitive ending. So the whole means 'hearts belonging to them'.
16.root: ق-ل-ب (q-l-b) — heart; to turn over, turn about, change

17.meaning: Say! — a command to speak or declare; the singular imperative addressed to one person.
17.grammar: Imperative (command) verb addressed to a single male/person: 'Say!'. From a hollow root, the middle weak letter drops in the command, leaving the short form 'qul'. The bare ending (no vowel) is characteristic of this singular imperative.

18.meaning: A compound meaning 'then whoever' or 'so whoever'. It combines 'then/so' with the conditional/relative 'who', introducing whatever person meets a stated condition.
18.grammar: The connector fa- ('then/so', often answering or following a condition) joined to man ('whoever / the one who'), which refers to people and introduces a condition: 'whoever does X…'. man does not change its ending; the clause after it supplies the rest of the meaning.

19.meaning: 'He/it owns, possesses, controls, has power over'. The verb conveys ownership and the authority/command that comes with it — to hold sway over something.

parts.en: owns / controls / has power over (with indicative -u)

19.grammar: A third-person masculine singular present-tense verb. The ya- prefix marks a 'he/it' subject, and the final -u is the indicative ending built into the stem, signalling an ongoing or actual action ('he owns / controls').
19.root: م-ل-ك (m-l-k) — to own, possess, hold dominion

20.meaning: 'For you' or 'to you' — the preposition of benefit or attribution ('for / belonging to') combined with a plural 'you', marking the people for whose benefit or possession something is done.
20.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The prefix la- (the preposition li- 'for', here vowelled 'la' before a pronoun) conveys benefit, purpose, or belonging. The suffix -kum is the second-person masculine plural object, 'you all'.

21.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
21.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

22.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
22.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

23.meaning: A thing; something or anything. With a negation it commonly amounts to 'nothing at all.'
23.grammar: A singular masculine noun, indefinite ('a thing'). The -an ending (tanwīn fatḥa) is the indefinite accusative, often used here as an object or an adverbial 'in any respect / at all.'

24.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
24.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

25.meaning: A verb meaning 'he intended', 'he willed', or 'he meant' — to direct one's purpose toward something, to want or aim at it.
25.grammar: Past-tense (perfect) verb, third-person masculine singular ('he'), in the derived (form IV) pattern arāda. The bare stem with a final -a denotes a completed action by a single male subject, with the sense of actively willing or purposing something.
25.root: ر-و-د (r-w-d) — to seek, want, aim at

26.meaning: A preposition 'bi' ('with / by / in / for') joined to the attached pronoun 'you all', yielding 'with you' or 'for you (plural)'. The exact shade — attachment, instrument, or benefit — depends on the verb it accompanies.
26.grammar: A preposition plus an attached pronoun. 'bi' is a versatile preposition (with, by, in, for), and -kum is the genitive/object pronoun 'you all' (masculine plural). Pronouns following a preposition always take this attached (genitive) form.

27.meaning: Harm / injury / hurt — that which damages or causes detriment; an affliction or adversity.
27.grammar: A noun. The final -an is 'nunation' (tanwīn) marking it as indefinite ('some harm / a harm'), and its -a vowel signals the accusative case — the ending typically used for the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon).
27.root: ض-ر-ر (ḍ-r-r) — harm, injury, damage, the opposite of benefit

28.meaning: Or — a particle offering an alternative or another option, linking two possibilities ('this… or that…'). It can also introduce an approximation or a different case.
28.grammar: A fixed connecting particle (a conjunction) with no case ending. It joins two words or clauses to present an alternative between them.

29.meaning: A verb meaning 'he intended', 'he willed', or 'he meant' — to direct one's purpose toward something, to want or aim at it.
29.grammar: Past-tense (perfect) verb, third-person masculine singular ('he'), in the derived (form IV) pattern arāda. The bare stem with a final -a denotes a completed action by a single male subject, with the sense of actively willing or purposing something.
29.root: ر-و-د (r-w-d) — to seek, want, aim at

30.meaning: A preposition 'bi' ('with / by / in / for') joined to the attached pronoun 'you all', yielding 'with you' or 'for you (plural)'. The exact shade — attachment, instrument, or benefit — depends on the verb it accompanies.
30.grammar: A preposition plus an attached pronoun. 'bi' is a versatile preposition (with, by, in, for), and -kum is the genitive/object pronoun 'you all' (masculine plural). Pronouns following a preposition always take this attached (genitive) form.

31.meaning: Benefit, profit, or advantage; something useful or gainful that brings good.
31.grammar: A singular noun marked indefinite ('benefit / some benefit'). The -an (tanwīn) combines the -a accusative case-ending — which typically marks the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon) — with the -n of indefiniteness.

32.meaning: A particle of retraction meaning 'rather,' 'no, but,' or 'nay' — it cancels or sets aside what was just said and shifts to a corrected or contrasting statement that follows.
32.grammar: An indeclinable particle (it never changes form). Its function is to redirect the discourse: it dismisses a prior idea and introduces what is actually the case.

33.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

33.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.

34.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
34.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

35.meaning: A phrase meaning 'in/with that which' or 'in what' — combining the sense of 'by means of' or 'concerning' with an unspecified thing ('whatever it may be').
35.grammar: The preposition bi ('in, with, by means of, concerning') attached to the relative/indefinite pronoun mā ('what, that which'). Both elements are invariable, so the phrase carries no case ending. A word governed by the preposition bi is understood to be in the genitive relationship.

36.meaning: You (all) do / work / act — to carry out deeds or labor.
36.grammar: A present-tense verb (Form I). The 'ta-' prefix with the '-ūna' ending marks the second-person masculine plural ('you all'). The '-ūna' (with final 'n') is the indicative form, marking a plain ongoing or habitual statement.
36.root: ع-م-ل (ʿ-m-l) — to do, work, act; deeds

37.meaning: Deeply aware, well-acquainted, fully informed — one whose knowledge penetrates the inner realities and hidden details of things. As a divine attribute of Allah, the All-Aware.
37.grammar: An adjective on the pattern faʿīl meaning 'thoroughly acquainted with inner realities.' The -an ending is the indefinite accusative: here it functions as a predicate complement ('… is all-aware') in clauses that take an accusative predicate, and the doubled nasal -n (tanwīn) shows it is indefinite.
37.root: خ-ب-ر (kh-b-r) — to know thoroughly, be acquainted with the inner truth of things; inner knowledge

1.meaning: A particle of retraction meaning 'rather,' 'no, but,' or 'nay' — it cancels or sets aside what was just said and shifts to a corrected or contrasting statement that follows.
1.grammar: An indeclinable particle (it never changes form). Its function is to redirect the discourse: it dismisses a prior idea and introduces what is actually the case.

2.meaning: You (plural) thought / you assumed — past tense, 2nd person plural: the belief or assumption held by those being addressed. In context, refers to the false assumption that the Prophet would not return from Hudaybiyyah.

parts.en: you (pl.) thought / assumed (2nd masc. pl. past)
