2.grammar: Past tense verb, 2nd person masculine plural, Form I. A doubled root (ظ-ن-ن) with assimilation of the doubled nūn.
2.root: ظ-ن-ن (ẓ-n-n) — to think, to assume; often with a sense of conjecture or false belief

3.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
3.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'
3.root: — (particle; no root)

4.meaning: A particle of strong negation directed at the future: 'never; will not at all.' It emphatically denies that something will ever happen and puts the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive.
4.grammar: A negating particle that governs a following present-tense verb, denying it for the future and forcing that verb into the subjunctive mood (so the verb takes a final '-a' instead of '-u'). It has no ending of its own.

5.meaning: He returns / would return — for something to revert or turn back. In the context of 48:12, refers to the Prophet turning back (not returning successfully from his mission).

parts.en: he returns / turns back (3rd masc. sg. subjunctive, Form VII)

5.grammar: Imperfect verb in the subjunctive mood, 3rd person masculine singular, Form VII (inqalaba — to turn back, to be overturned). The -a ending marks the subjunctive.
5.root: ق-ل-ب (q-l-b) — to turn over, to flip; Form VII: to be turned over, to return, to revert

6.meaning: 'The Messenger' — one sent with a message; in religious usage, a prophet commissioned by Allah to deliver revelation to people.
6.grammar: 'al-' is the definite article 'the' (its 'l' assimilates into the following r, doubling it). 'rasūl' is a noun meaning 'one who is sent, an envoy/messenger'. The final -u is the nominative ending, the case typically marking the subject of a sentence or a word simply being named.
6.root: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — sending, dispatching, a message/envoy

7.meaning: "and the believers" — those who have faith, who accept and trust; wa- joins it on and al- makes it definite ('the believers' as a group).
7.grammar: A masculine sound plural noun, 'believers.' The -ūna ending is the subject (nominative) form of the masculine plural, used when the word is the one doing the action; the matching object/possessive form would be -īna.
7.root: ء-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — safety, security, faith, trust

8.meaning: "to / towards" — a preposition marking the end-point, goal, or direction of a movement or extent ("up to," "as far as," "toward").
8.grammar: An indeclinable preposition; it has no case ending of its own and always governs a following noun in the genitive case.

9.meaning: Their families — those belonging to them, the people of their households. Refers to the families of those returning from Hudaybiyyah.
9.grammar: Masculine irregular plural of ahl, in the genitive/accusative (oblique) case (/-ī/ oblique form of the sound masculine plural ending), with 3rd person masculine plural possessive suffix -him.
9.root: أ-ه-ل (ʾ-h-l) — family, people; ahlīhim = their families

10.meaning: An adverb meaning 'ever / forever / at any time' — used to stress that something will never (or always) be the case throughout all time, especially with a negative to mean 'never, not ever'.
10.grammar: A noun used adverbially. The ending -an is the indefinite accusative, the form regularly used to turn a word into an adverb of time ('… ever / forever'); the -n (nunation) marks it as indefinite. Paired with a negation it strengthens it to 'never, not ever'.

11.meaning: And it was made to seem fair / was adorned in their eyes — a passive construction: something (staying behind) was beautified and made attractive to them, i.e. Satan or their own desires decorated it for them.

parts.en: was adorned / was made fair-seeming (3rd masc. sg. passive past, Form II)

11.grammar: Conjunction wāw + past tense passive verb, 3rd person masculine singular, Form II (zayyanaزَيَّنَ → passive zuyyina).
11.root: ز-ي-ن (z-y-n) — to adorn, to beautify; passive: to be made to seem beautiful / fair

12.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that' — pointing to something regarded as distant or elevated, as opposed to 'this' (hadha) for what is near. It singles out a masculine singular thing and lends it a sense of distinction or loftiness.
12.grammar: A demonstrative for a masculine singular referent at a distance. The -ka ending is an address particle directed at a single male listener; it does not change for case. The whole word stays fixed in form regardless of its grammatical position.

13.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
13.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

14.meaning: Your hearts — the inner seat of feeling, intention, and understanding, belonging to a group of people.
14.grammar: A plural noun 'hearts' carrying the -i (genitive) ending because it is the first term of a possessive (iḍāfa) construction with the following pronoun -kum ('your', for a group). This noun-plus-pronoun pairing expresses possession: 'the hearts OF you all' = 'your hearts'. In Arabic the heart is understood as the center of both emotion and thought.
14.root: ق-ل-ب (q-l-b) — heart; to turn over, change

15.meaning: And you (plural) assumed — same as ẓanantum but with the conjunction wāw preceding it, linking this assumption to the previous one. The repeated accusation of false assumption emphasises the gravity of the hypocrites' misjudgment.
15.grammar: Conjunction wāw + past tense verb, 2nd person masculine plural, Form I (ẓanna), doubled root.
15.root: ظ-ن-ن (ẓ-n-n) — to think, to assume wrongly

16.meaning: Conjecture, supposition, opinion, or assumption — a thought held with less than certainty. Depending on context it ranges from reasonable supposition to baseless guesswork; here it is the noun "thinking/assumption."
16.grammar: A noun with the -a ending, which is accusative. This ending typically marks the noun as the direct object of a verb, or as the first term in a tightly-bound "… of …" possessive phrase when it leads into a following genitive noun.
16.root: ظ-ن-ن (ẓ-n-n) — to suppose, conjecture, think; holding an opinion short of certainty

17.meaning: 'The evil, the bad, the harmful' — that which is wicked, woeful, or calamitous; misfortune and ill. As a noun it denotes badness or harm in general.
17.grammar: A noun made definite by al- ('the'). The final -i is the genitive case: it typically links the word to a preceding noun ('the … OF evil') or follows a preposition. Here the genitive marks it as the second term of a possessive phrase ('the … of evil').
17.root: س-و-ء (s-w-ʾ) — to be bad/evil; harm, misfortune

18.meaning: And you (plural) were — reporting a past state or ongoing condition of a group of people.
18.grammar: The connector 'and' attached to the past tense of the verb 'to be'. The ending -tum marks 'you all' (masculine plural) as the subject. This verb sets up a description of a state in the past ('you all were …'), and it typically introduces the condition or situation that followed.
18.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist, to come into being

19.meaning: 'A people, a folk, a community' — a group of human beings bound together, often by kinship, tribe, or shared standing.
19.grammar: An indefinite collective noun. The -an ending (accusative with tanwīn, the 'n' sound) marks it as the object of an action.
19.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise; a standing group, people

20.meaning: Ruined / destroyed — a state of loss and ruin; those who are utterly destroyed. Used as a predicate indicating the wretched condition of those who were faithless.
20.grammar: Indefinite noun/adjective in the accusative case (manṣūb) used as a predicate or ḥāl. May be singular or plural (buwar — ruined people).
20.root: ب-و-ر (b-w-r) — to be ruined, to perish; bawār = ruin, destruction

1.meaning: And whoever / and the one who — a joining word plus a relative pronoun introducing a person (or persons) defined by whatever they do; often sets up a condition ('whoever does X …').
1.grammar: A particle 'and' joined to the relative/conditional pronoun man ('whoever, who'). Man does not change its ending; it refers to people and frequently functions as a conditional, so the verb that follows it typically takes the shortened jussive mood.

2.meaning: The particle 'lam', a negating word used to push a verb into the past: it means 'did not' / 'has not'. Though it sits before a present-tense verb form, it negates the action as something that did not happen.
2.grammar: 'lam' is a negating particle that governs a following present-tense verb but gives it past meaning ('did not …'). It also puts that verb into the shortened (jussive) form. 'lam' itself carries no ending.

3.meaning: He believes, has faith, trusts and affirms as true — inwardly accepting and giving secure assent, the core act of faith.
3.grammar: A present-tense verb in the causative (Form IV, أَفْعَلَ) pattern. The yu- prefix means 'he'. The vowel-less final -n marks the jussive mood, the clipped form a verb takes after certain particles (such as negation or conditions) rather than the plain ongoing form.
3.root: أ-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — safety, trust, faith, security

4.meaning: A phrase 'in Allah / by Allah', combining the preposition 'with/in/by' and the divine name Allah, the proper name of the One God.
4.grammar: The preposition bi- ('in, with, by means of') prefixed to the divine name Allah. A preposition always forces the following noun into the genitive case, which is why Allah here ends in -i. With verbs of believing, bi- conveys the object of faith — to believe IN.
4.root: — (Allah is the proper name of God and is not derived from a triliteral root in the usual sense)

5.meaning: A phrase meaning 'and His Messenger' — referring to one who is sent, an envoy or apostle bearing a message, joined by 'and' and possessed by 'His.'
5.grammar: 'Messenger' joined by wa- ('and') and followed by the possessive pronoun -hi ('his'). The -i vowel before the pronoun is the genitive case, here because the word is linked in possession ('Messenger OF Him'); the pronoun takes the -hi form (with i-vowel) when it follows an i-sound.
5.root: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — sending, dispatching; a message or one who is sent

6.meaning: Then indeed we: 'we' stated with emphasis and a connecting 'then/so'. The particle inna strongly affirms the statement, while the prefix fa- ties it as a consequence to what came before.
6.grammar: The connective fa- ('then, so', often marking a result) prefixed to the emphasizing particle inna ('indeed, truly'), with the attached first-person plural pronoun -nā meaning 'we/us' (the doubled nūn shared between inna and the pronoun is written once as a shadda). After inna a pronoun takes this object-style form. The whole emphatically asserts a statement about 'we' as a consequence.

7.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'we made ready / we prepared in advance,' conveying the deliberate arranging or setting-up of something beforehand so that it stands ready.

parts.en: (part of the stem; the verb is from the form-IV pattern aʿtada)

7.grammar: A completed (past-tense) action verb. The attached -nā ending is the 'we' subject marker, telling you the doers are first-person plural. As a past-tense form it presents the action as already finished and accomplished.
7.root: ع-ت-د (ʿ-t-d) — readiness, preparing/making something ready

8.meaning: A three-part word: 'for' + 'the' + 'those who cover up the truth / reject faith.' The base noun denotes the kāfir — one who disbelieves, denies, and ungratefully conceals the truth and Allah's favor. With 'for,' it marks them as the ones for whom something is intended.
8.grammar: The preposition 'li-' ('for/to') joined to a definite plural noun, masculine. The '-īna' ending is the sound masculine plural in its genitive/accusative (oblique) form, here required because it follows the preposition 'li-'. The whole denotes 'for the disbelievers.'
8.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal, disbelieve, be ungrateful

9.meaning: A blazing, fiercely kindled fire — flame that has been set ablaze and roars with intensity. The form conveys a fire that is made to burn violently.
9.grammar: A noun/intensive adjective. The final -an (tanwīn fatḥ) marks it as indefinite and in the accusative case, which typically signals a direct object or a descriptive complement governed into the accusative.
9.root: س-ع-ر (s-ʿ-r) — to kindle, to set ablaze, to make a fire flare up

1.meaning: A phrase meaning 'and to Allah (belongs)' — expressing ownership or rightful belonging to Allah; the lām conveys possession or entitlement.
1.grammar: The conjunction 'wa-' ('and') joined to the prepositional phrase 'lillāhi'. This phrase is the preposition 'li-' ('to/for', here showing possession) prefixed to the name 'Allah'; when 'li-' attaches, the connecting hamza and the first lām of the definite article are elided in writing, leaving a single written lām for the preposition followed by the doubled (shadda-bearing) lām of the name. 'Allah' takes the -i (genitive) ending required after a preposition.

2.meaning: Kingdom, dominion, sovereign rule — full ownership and authority over a realm; the right and power to command and dispose.
2.grammar: A singular noun. The final -u marks the nominative case, used when the noun is the subject of a sentence or the thing being identified ('the dominion is …'). The absence of nunation here points to its being made definite by a following possessor in a genitive link.
2.root: م-ل-ك (m-l-k) — to own, rule; kingship, dominion

3.meaning: The heavens / the skies — the plural of 'heaven', referring to the skies above and the celestial realms; the elevated expanse over the earth.
3.grammar: A definite feminine plural noun with the prefix 'al-' ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the heavens') or follows a preposition. In the sound feminine plural, this -i form also covers what would be an object role.
3.root: س-م-و (s-m-w) — height, sky

4.meaning: 'And the earth' — the connective 'and' joined to 'the earth', meaning the ground, land, or the world beneath the sky.
4.grammar: The connective 'wa-' ('and') with the definite feminine noun 'al-arḍ' ('the earth'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the earth') or follows a preposition, here matching the case of what it is joined to.
4.root: أ-ر-ض (ʾ-r-ḍ) — earth, land

5.meaning: 'He forgives / pardons' — to cover over and wipe away sins, granting protective pardon. The root carries the image of covering a fault so it is no longer held against a person.
5.grammar: A present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he'). The separate final -u is the indicative ending, marking a plain, ongoing statement of fact ('he forgives').

6.meaning: 'for whoever / to the one who' — the preposition 'for/to' joined with the relative word 'who', introducing the person(s) about whom something is said.
6.grammar: A preposition ('for/to') combined with the relative/interrogative word 'man' ('who, whoever'). Together they single out a person or group as the focus ('for the one(s) who...').

7.meaning: A present-tense verb meaning 'he wills, he wishes, he chooses' — to want or intend something by one's own decision.
7.grammar: A present/ongoing action by a single masculine subject ('he'); the ya- prefix marks third-person masculine singular, and the final -u marks the indicative mood — a plain statement of fact ('he wills'), as opposed to a command or a verb governed by 'that.'
7.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʾ) — willing, wishing; the root behind 'thing' (shayʾ)

8.meaning: "and He punishes / and He will torment" — the prefix wa- joins this to what precedes; the verb itself means to subject someone to painful chastisement or torment. The doubled middle consonant gives an intensive, deliberate sense (to inflict severe, drawn-out suffering).
8.grammar: Present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he'). The yu- prefix marks 'he' in a derived (intensive) form, and the final -u ending marks the ordinary (indicative) present, signalling an action that is ongoing or yet to happen ('he punishes / he will punish').
8.root: ع-ذ-ب (ʿ-dh-b) — pain, torment, chastisement

9.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
9.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.
9.root: — (pronoun)

10.meaning: A present-tense verb meaning 'he wills, he wishes, he chooses' — to want or intend something by one's own decision.
10.grammar: A present/ongoing action by a single masculine subject ('he'); the ya- prefix marks third-person masculine singular, and the final -u marks the indicative mood — a plain statement of fact ('he wills'), as opposed to a command or a verb governed by 'that.'
10.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʾ) — willing, wishing; the root behind 'thing' (shayʾ)

11.meaning: And he was / he became — a verb of being that places a subject in a past state or links it to a description in the past.
11.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'kāna' is a past-tense verb, 3rd-person masculine singular, meaning 'he was/became'; it commonly introduces a past condition and is typically followed by a noun describing the subject's state. The final -a marks completed past action by a single male.

12.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
12.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

13.meaning: A word meaning 'much-forgiving' or 'ever-forgiving' — an intensive form describing one whose forgiveness is abundant and constant. It is one of the qualities of Allah.
13.grammar: An intensive adjective on the pattern faʿūl, conveying that the quality is great in degree and repeated. The ending -an is the accusative case with tanwīn (the indefinite 'n' sound), written with a supporting alif; it is the form an indefinite word takes when it is, for example, a predicate of certain verbs/particles or otherwise placed in the object position.

14.meaning: 'Most Merciful / deeply compassionate' — an intensive form of raḥima, denoting one full of mercy and tender compassion; a frequent description of Allah.
14.grammar: An intensive adjective on the fa'īl pattern, expressing a deep, abiding quality — abounding in mercy. The -an ending is the accusative case with indefinite (tanwīn) 'n,' often marking it as a predicate or as describing someone as 'most merciful.'

1.meaning: 'He/it will say' — a statement of future speech. Built from the present-tense verb 'he says' with the prefixed particle sa- ('will, shall, is going to'), marking an action expected to happen soon.
1.grammar: The prefix sa- places the verb in the near future ('will say'). The base verb is present-tense, third-person masculine singular: the ya- prefix means 'he', and the final -u ending marks the indicative mood (a plain, factual statement, as opposed to commands or subjunctive forms).

2.meaning: Those left behind / kept back: people who were caused to remain behind while others went forth, held back from joining an undertaking.

parts.en: ones left behind (passive participle, Form II, plural)

2.grammar: A passive participle ('the ones who were …') with the definite article al- ('the'). The sound masculine plural ending here is -ūna, which marks the word as the subject (the doer/topic) rather than an object. Being passive, it names a group to whom something was done — they were left behind.
2.root: خ-ل-ف (kh-l-f) — to come after, be left behind, remain in the rear

3.meaning: 'When' — a particle introducing a time or circumstance, generally pointing to something expected or definite to come ('when/whenever it happens'). It sets up a condition or moment whose outcome then follows.
3.grammar: An indeclinable adverb/particle of time; it has no case ending and never changes form. It typically introduces a clause about a future or recurring event ('when …'), and is normally followed by a verb describing what takes place.
3.root: — (a time particle; no triliteral root)

4.meaning: You (plural) set out / departed — you started your journey, marched forward. Refers to setting out on an expedition or journey with determination.

parts.en: you (pl.) set forth / departed (2nd masc. pl. past, Form VII)

4.grammar: Past tense verb, 2nd person masculine plural, Form VII (inṭalaqa — to set off, to depart freely).
4.root: ط-ل-ق (ṭ-l-q) — to be free, to release; Form VII: to set forth, to depart, to set off

5.meaning: A preposition meaning 'to,' 'toward,' or 'up to' — pointing to the end-point, goal, or limit of a motion, direction, or extent.
5.grammar: A preposition (a small linking word). It governs the noun after it, putting that noun in the genitive case, and points to a destination or limit ('to,' 'toward,' 'as far as').

6.meaning: Spoils of war, war-booty — the goods and wealth captured from the enemy after a battle. Plural of maghnam. In the context of 48:15, the Bedouin who stayed behind hope to take the spoils of Khaybar.

parts.en: spoils of war / booty (indefinite plural accusative, diptote)

6.grammar: Broken plural of maghnam (مَغْنَم), in the accusative case (manṣūb), diptote (no tanwīn).
6.root: غ-ن-م (gh-n-m) — to gain, to profit; ghaniīma/maghnam = war-booty, spoils; ghunm = gain

7.meaning: To take it — so that you would take/receive it (the spoils). Purpose clause expressing the intention of the stay-behinds in wanting to follow the believers.

parts.en: you (pl.) may take (2nd masc. pl. subjunctive)

7.grammar: Lām of purpose + imperfect verb in subjunctive mood, 2nd person masculine plural (Form I: akhadha), with 3rd person feminine singular object pronoun (referring to maghānim or the booty).
7.root: أ-خ-ذ (ʾ-kh-dh) — to take, to seize, to receive

8.meaning: Allow us / let us — an imperative: 'leave us' or 'let us come along.' The Bedouin asking the believers to allow them to follow them to get the spoils.

parts.en: allow us / let us (2nd masc. pl. imperative with 1st pl. object pronoun)

8.grammar: Imperative mood, 2nd person masculine plural of the verb dharaوَذَر (to leave/allow), an irregular verb with no māḍī in standard use. Attached 1st person plural object pronoun -nā.
8.root: و-ذ-ر (w-dh-r) — to leave, to allow; imperative dharu = let!, allow!

9.meaning: We follow you — we come along behind you. Present tense, 1st person plural: the Bedouin's stated desire to accompany the believers for the purpose of getting the spoils.

parts.en: we follow (1st pl. imperfect, jussive form)

9.grammar: Imperfect verb in jussive mood (majzūm, by implication after dharūnā), 1st person plural, Form VIII (ittabaʿa — to follow after), with attached 2nd person masculine plural object pronoun.
9.root: ت-ب-ع (t-b-ʿ) — to follow; Form VIII: to follow closely, to conform

10.meaning: they want / they intend — to will, desire, or purpose something. The verb conveys an active, ongoing intention or wish on the part of a group.
10.grammar: A present-tense Form IV verb (arāda, 'to will/intend'). The yu- prefix marks a third-person subject, and the ending -ūna marks masculine plural plus the indicative mood (a plain statement: 'they want'). The -na would drop under a particle that changes the mood.

11.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
11.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

12.meaning: They change / they alter — referring to those who would want to alter the words of Allah. The Qur'an states that no one can change Allah's words.

parts.en: they change / alter (3rd masc. pl. subjunctive, Form II)

12.grammar: Imperfect verb in subjunctive mood, 3rd person masculine plural, Form II (baddala — to change, alter, substitute). Wāw of plural (ū) marks the subjunctive.
12.root: ب-د-ل (b-d-l) — to change, to exchange; Form II: to alter, to substitute

13.meaning: The words / the speech — referring to the Words (kalām) of Allah, His decrees and statements that no one has the power to change or alter.
13.grammar: Masculine noun in the accusative case (manṣūb) in construct (iḍāfa) with Allāh.
13.root: ك-ل-م (k-l-m) — to speak; kalām = speech, words, discourse

14.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
14.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

15.meaning: An imperative command meaning 'Say!' or 'Speak!' — a direct order to one person to utter or declare something.
15.grammar: A command (imperative) verb addressed to a single male. The bare, vowelless ending (the silent stop on the final 'l') marks it as a direct order: 'you, say!' It is built from the verb 'to say' with the weak middle letter dropped, leaving the short, clipped command form.
15.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — to say, to speak, to utter

16.meaning: A particle of strong negation directed at the future: 'never; will not at all.' It emphatically denies that something will ever happen and puts the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive.
16.grammar: A negating particle that governs a following present-tense verb, denying it for the future and forcing that verb into the subjunctive mood (so the verb takes a final '-a' instead of '-u'). It has no ending of its own.

17.meaning: Will you follow us — a question addressed to the stay-behinds: 'Are you saying that you will now follow us?' Expressing doubt about the sincerity of their stated willingness.

parts.en: you (pl.) will follow us (2nd masc. pl. imperfect indicative + 1st pl. object pronoun)

17.grammar: Imperfect verb, indicative mood, 2nd person masculine plural, Form VIII (ittabaʿa), with attached 1st person plural object pronoun -nā. Marked by /-ūna/ + -nā.
17.root: ت-ب-ع (t-b-ʿ) — to follow; Form VIII: to follow closely

18.meaning: Thus / in that manner — a demonstrative adverb meaning 'like that, in this way.' Pointing back to what was just described as a comparison or conclusion.

parts.en: thus / like that (demonstrative adverb for a group being addressed)

18.grammar: Comparative particle ka + demonstrative pronoun dhālikum (that — for a group being addressed). Functions as an adverb of manner.

19.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
19.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.

20.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
20.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

21.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
21.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

22.meaning: An adverb of time meaning 'before / beforehand / previously,' pointing to a moment or state that precedes something else in time. When used with the final vowel -u (qablu), it stands cut off from an explicit following noun, conveying 'before(hand)' or 'previously' in an absolute sense — the thing it is 'before' is understood rather than stated.
22.grammar: An adverb of time. The final -u ending here is the indeclinable (mabnī) form taken when the word is severed from a following genitive: rather than 'before X,' it means 'before(hand)' on its own, with the reference point left implicit.
22.root: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l) — to come before, precede, be in front; to receive/accept

23.meaning: Then they will say — a verb of speaking set in the future, declaring that a group will speak; 'then/so they are going to say.'
23.grammar: Layered prefixes: fa- ('then'), sa- ('will,' marking the future). The verb is present-tense with ya-…-ūna for 'they' (plural masculine). The full -ūna ending is the indicative form, used for a plain statement (not a command or negated form).

24.meaning: A particle of retraction meaning 'rather,' 'no, but,' or 'nay' — it cancels or sets aside what was just said and shifts to a corrected or contrasting statement that follows.
24.grammar: An indeclinable particle (it never changes form). Its function is to redirect the discourse: it dismisses a prior idea and introduces what is actually the case.

25.meaning: You envy us — a taunt or accusation: 'Are you jealous of us?' Referring to the Bedouin's supposed envy of the believers who were invited to go on the next expedition.

parts.en: you (pl.) envy us (2nd masc. pl. imperfect indicative + 1st pl. object pronoun)

25.grammar: Imperfect verb, indicative mood, 2nd person masculine plural, Form I (ḥasada — to envy), with attached 1st person plural object pronoun -nā.
25.root: ح-س-د (ḥ-s-d) — to envy, to begrudge; ḥasad = envy

26.meaning: A particle of retraction meaning 'rather,' 'no, but,' or 'nay' — it cancels or sets aside what was just said and shifts to a corrected or contrasting statement that follows.
26.grammar: An indeclinable particle (it never changes form). Its function is to redirect the discourse: it dismisses a prior idea and introduces what is actually the case.

27.meaning: 'They were' or 'they used to' — a past-tense form of the verb 'to be' for a group. It often expresses a continued or habitual state in the past, especially when paired with a following verb ('they used to do...').
27.grammar: A past-tense verb from the verb 'to be'. The -ū ending marks the third-person masculine plural subject, 'they'. As a past form of 'to be', it sets a past frame; with a following present-tense verb it typically conveys a habitual or ongoing past ('they used to...').
27.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

28.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
28.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

29.meaning: Verb meaning 'they understand / comprehend deeply' — to grasp the inner meaning of something with discernment, a perceptive, penetrating understanding.
29.grammar: A present-tense verb, masculine third-person plural. The complete '-ūna' ending (with the 'nūn' intact) signals the indicative mood — a plain ongoing statement, 'they understand.' The root connotes deep, discerning comprehension rather than mere hearing.
29.root: ف-ق-ه (f-q-h) — to understand deeply, comprehend with insight (source of the word fiqh)

30.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
30.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

31.meaning: 'A little / a small amount' — an adjective/noun meaning small in quantity, few, scant, or trifling.
31.grammar: A noun/adjective 'little' in the accusative case with indefinite marking (the -an ending, tanwīn). The accusative commonly marks an object or specifies amount/manner; the doubled -n sound marks it as indefinite, 'a little.'
31.root: ق-ل-ل (q-l-l) — fewness; being little, scant, or small in amount

1.meaning: An imperative command meaning 'Say!' or 'Speak!' — a direct order to one person to utter or declare something.
1.grammar: A command (imperative) verb addressed to a single male. The bare, vowelless ending (the silent stop on the final 'l') marks it as a direct order: 'you, say!' It is built from the verb 'to say' with the weak middle letter dropped, leaving the short, clipped command form.
1.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — to say, to speak, to utter

2.meaning: To / for those who stayed behind — the laggards who did not join the Prophet; those left behind while the believers went on expedition.

parts.en: those who stayed behind / were left behind (masculine plural oblique)

2.grammar: Preposition lām + definite article + passive participle Form II (khallafa → mukhallaf — one who is left behind), masculine sound plural in oblique case (/-īna/).
2.root: خ-ل-ف (kh-l-f) — to stay behind, to succeed; Form II passive: mukhallaf = one left behind

3.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
3.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

4.meaning: The bedouins; the desert-dwelling Arabs of the open country, as distinct from settled town-dwellers. A collective noun referring to nomadic Arab tribes.
4.grammar: A definite collective noun (plural pattern afʿāl) used for desert Arabs. The -i ending is genitive: it marks the word as following a preposition or linked to a preceding noun ('... of ...').
4.root: ع-ر-ب (ʿ-r-b) — Arab; clear, articulate speech

5.meaning: You (plural) will be called — a future passive: they will be summoned/called upon (to fight a powerful enemy). Indicates that their test is not over; there will be another call to arms.

parts.en: you (pl.) will be called / summoned (2nd masc. pl. future passive)

5.grammar: Future particle sa + imperfect passive verb, 2nd person masculine plural (Form I daʿā passive). Marked by /-awna/ passive plural ending.
5.root: د-ع-و (d-ʿ-w) — to call, to invite, to summon; passive: to be called

6.meaning: A preposition meaning 'to,' 'toward,' or 'up to' — pointing to the end-point, goal, or limit of a motion, direction, or extent.
6.grammar: A preposition (a small linking word). It governs the noun after it, putting that noun in the genitive case, and points to a destination or limit ('to,' 'toward,' 'as far as').

7.meaning: A people, folk, or community — a group of persons bound together (often by kinship or shared identity); a nation or tribe.
7.grammar: A singular collective noun (grammatically masculine, referring to a group). The final -in is the genitive case with nunation (tanwīn), marking it indefinite ('a people'); the genitive typically follows a preposition or links to a preceding noun ('… of a people').
7.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise, establish; a standing group of people

8.meaning: Possessors of / those endowed with. A word meaning 'owners of' or 'people having' some quality, used to attribute a trait or rank to a group.
8.grammar: A noun meaning 'possessors/people of', which has no singular from its own letters (its singular is supplied by another word). The 'ī' ending here reflects its non-nominative (genitive/accusative) form and it is always followed by a noun naming what is possessed ('possessors OF …').

9.meaning: Might, force, valour in war — formidable strength and the harm or violence it can inflict; also hardship or adversity.
9.grammar: A noun denoting forceful power or distress. The final -in (with tanwīn) is the indefinite genitive ending: a noun takes this state after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun as 'a … of …'.
9.root: ب-أ-س (b-ʾ-s) — force, might; hardship, adversity

10.meaning: An adjective meaning 'strong, mighty, intense, severe, firm' — describing something powerful and hard to overcome.
10.grammar: Singular indefinite adjective on the intensive faʿīl pattern. The '-in' ending marks it indefinite and genitive, agreeing with an indefinite genitive noun it describes ('a strong …').
10.root: ش-د-د (sh-d-d) — to be strong, intense, firm, severe

11.meaning: You (plural) fight them — present/future tense: you will engage in battle against them. Refers to a future conflict the believers will face.

parts.en: you (pl.) fight them (2nd masc. pl. imperfect, Form III)

11.grammar: Imperfect verb, indicative mood, 2nd person masculine plural, Form III (qātala — to fight against), with attached 3rd person masculine plural object pronoun.
11.root: ق-ت-ل (q-t-l) — to kill; Form III: to fight against (reciprocal combat)

12.meaning: Or — a particle offering an alternative or another option, linking two possibilities ('this… or that…'). It can also introduce an approximation or a different case.
12.grammar: A fixed connecting particle (a conjunction) with no case ending. It joins two words or clauses to present an alternative between them.

13.meaning: They submit / they accept Islam — they give in and yield (either through conversion or surrender). Refers to the enemy capitulating, either militarily or by accepting Islam.

parts.en: they submit / accept Islam (3rd masc. pl. imperfect, Form IV)

13.grammar: Imperfect verb, indicative mood, 3rd person masculine plural, Form IV (aslama — to submit, to enter Islam). Marked by /-ūna/.
13.root: س-ل-م (s-l-m) — peace, safety; Form IV: to submit, to surrender, to accept Islam (islām)

14.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'fa-' ('then', 'so', 'but') drawing a consequence, joined to the conditional particle 'in' ('if'). Together: 'then if …', 'but if …'.
14.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector that signals a result or transition ('then/so'). 'in' is the conditional particle 'if', introducing a supposed condition. Both are indeclinable particles with no case ending.

15.meaning: Addressed to a group: 'you obey / comply with / heed' — to follow another's command willingly and submissively.
15.grammar: A present-tense verb in a stem (form IV, 'a-…') meaning to render obedience. The '-ū' ending (without a final 'na') shows the group form 'you all' in the subjunctive or jussive mood — the form used after certain particles such as 'if' or 'not', or to express a dependent/conditional sense.
15.root: ط-و-ع (ṭ-w-ʿ) — to obey, comply, submit willingly

16.meaning: Allah will give you — He will bestow upon you (plural). Refers to the divine reward Allah will grant to those who obey and fight in His cause.

parts.en: He will give (3rd masc. sg. imperfect, Form IV, jussive)
you (2nd masc. pl. object pronoun, with liaison vowel)

16.grammar: Imperfect verb, 3rd person masculine singular, Form IV (ātā → yu'tī — to give), in jussive form (no -ī ending), with attached 2nd person masculine plural object pronoun -kumu.
16.root: أ-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come; Form IV: to give, to bestow

17.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
17.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

18.meaning: A reward, wage, or recompense — the return earned for work or conduct, whether worldly pay or otherworldly recompense.
18.grammar: A noun meaning 'a reward.' The final '-an' (tanwīn fatḥa) marks the indefinite accusative case, the case used for the object of a verb (e.g. of 'to give'), giving the sense 'a reward.'
18.root: ا-ج-ر (ʾ-j-r) — reward, wage, recompense for what one does

19.meaning: Good, fine, beautiful, excellent — pleasing and praiseworthy in quality. It describes something done well or possessing goodness and beauty.
19.grammar: An adjective ('good'). The -an ending is accusative with 'tanwīn' (-n, indefinite). As an adjective it agrees with and describes a noun; the accusative case matches a noun in that same case.

20.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'wa-' ('and'), joined to 'in', the conditional particle meaning 'if'. Together: 'and if …'.
20.grammar: 'wa-' is a connecting particle ('and'). 'in' is a particle introducing a hypothetical condition ('if …'), typically setting up a result clause that follows. Neither carries a case ending.

21.meaning: 'You turn away' / 'you turn your backs' — to turn aside, retreat, or shun, often implying rejecting or abandoning something. Addressed to a group.
21.grammar: A present-tense verb (Form V, 'to turn oneself away') addressed to a group of males ('you all'). The 'ta-' prefix marks the second person, and the final '-aw/-ū' element marks the plural subject. The shortened form (without a final 'n') signals the subjunctive/jussive — used after particles like 'if' or 'lest,' giving a sense such as 'if you turn away.'
21.root: و-ل-ي (w-l-y) — to be near; to turn toward or away, take charge

22.meaning: 'Just as / in the same way that' — a phrase of comparison joining 'like / as' to 'what', meaning 'like that which...' or 'in the manner that...'.
22.grammar: The comparison particle ka- ('like / as') joined to mā ('what / that which'). Together they introduce a likeness or manner — 'just as...', 'in the same way that...' — comparing one thing or action to another.

23.meaning: "You turned away / turned your backs / took charge" — the verb means to turn away, turn aside, or turn one's back; in another sense to take charge of or befriend. The form carries a 'you' (plural) subject.
23.grammar: A past-tense reflexive/intensive verb with the attached subject suffix '-tum' ('you all'), marking a completed action done by the plural addressees. The '-tum' ending is what makes the verb mean 'you (all) did it'.
23.root: و-ل-ي (w-l-y) — to be near / turn toward or away / take charge

24.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
24.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

25.meaning: An adverb of time meaning 'before / beforehand / previously,' pointing to a moment or state that precedes something else in time. When used with the final vowel -u (qablu), it stands cut off from an explicit following noun, conveying 'before(hand)' or 'previously' in an absolute sense — the thing it is 'before' is understood rather than stated.
25.grammar: An adverb of time. The final -u ending here is the indeclinable (mabnī) form taken when the word is severed from a following genitive: rather than 'before X,' it means 'before(hand)' on its own, with the reference point left implicit.
25.root: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l) — to come before, precede, be in front; to receive/accept

26.meaning: "he/He will punish you (plural)" — to inflict chastisement or torment. The verb is the intensive 'to punish severely', with 'you all' attached as its object.
26.grammar: A present-tense intensive verb (form II), 3rd-person masculine singular, with an attached object pronoun. The yu- prefix means 'he'. The verb stem ends in a vowelless (sukūn) state, the mark of the jussive mood — the clipped form used after conditional or commanding particles. The suffix -kum means 'you all' as the ones acted upon. The doubled middle root letter gives the intensive 'to punish'.

27.meaning: 'A punishment / torment.' A noun naming chastisement or painful suffering inflicted as a penalty.
27.grammar: A masculine noun. The -an ending marks it as indefinite ('a punishment') and in the accusative case — the form a noun takes as the object of a verb or as the thing being described/quantified.

28.meaning: An adjective meaning 'painful, agonizing, causing severe pain,' describing something that inflicts intense suffering.
28.grammar: An adjective in the intensive faʿīl pattern, which heightens the quality (deeply/intensely painful). The final -an (tanwīn fatḥa) marks it as indefinite ('a painful one') and in the accusative case — the case typically used for the object of a verb or for a describing word agreeing with such a noun.

1.meaning: A special negating verb meaning 'is not / are not'. Unlike a simple particle, it behaves like a verb (frozen in the past-tense form) and serves to deny that something is the case, cancelling an assertion of being.
1.grammar: A defective verb fixed in the 3rd-person masculine singular ('he/it is not'). The final -a is its frozen ending; it does not conjugate for tense like other verbs. Grammatically it raises its subject to the nominative and puts its predicate in the accusative, functioning to negate a state of being.

2.meaning: 'To / before / upon' — a preposition whose core sense is being on top of, above, or directed onto something; with a verb of presenting it carries the directional sense 'to / before / in front of,' and it can also convey obligation ('incumbent upon').
2.grammar: A preposition. Its basic meaning is 'on, upon, over,' but with verbs of displaying or presenting it shades into 'to / before / in front of.' It governs the following noun in the genitive case. It is fixed in form and takes no changing ending of its own (its final long -ā is an unchanging part of the word).
2.root: — (preposition; loosely related to the sense of 'height/elevation')

3.meaning: 'The blind one' — a person lacking sight. Often used figuratively for one who cannot perceive truth or guidance.
3.grammar: A definite descriptive noun/adjective ('the blind') marked by 'al-' ('the'), built on the pattern used for colours and bodily traits. It ends in a fixed long '-ā' vowel and does not change its ending for case — the form stays the same whether subject or object.
3.root: ع-م-ي (ʿ-m-y) — blindness, loss of sight or insight

4.meaning: Tightness, constriction, or distress of the heart — a sense of being hemmed in, hence unease, difficulty, or the kind of moral discomfort felt when something weighs on one. By extension it can mean blame or sin that constricts the conscience.
4.grammar: The -un ending (nunation) marks an indefinite noun ('a ___ / any ___') in the nominative case, the case typically used for the subject of a sentence or the thing being described as existing.
4.root: ح-ر-ج (ḥ-r-j) — narrowness, constriction, difficulty

5.meaning: 'And not' — a connector 'and' joined to the negative particle 'not,' negating a following statement.
5.grammar: Two particles: the joining 'and' (wa) plus the negator lā ('not'). Lā commonly negates a present-tense verb or a noun. Neither particle takes case endings.

6.meaning: 'To / before / upon' — a preposition whose core sense is being on top of, above, or directed onto something; with a verb of presenting it carries the directional sense 'to / before / in front of,' and it can also convey obligation ('incumbent upon').
6.grammar: A preposition. Its basic meaning is 'on, upon, over,' but with verbs of displaying or presenting it shades into 'to / before / in front of.' It governs the following noun in the genitive case. It is fixed in form and takes no changing ending of its own (its final long -ā is an unchanging part of the word).
6.root: — (preposition; loosely related to the sense of 'height/elevation')

7.meaning: The lame — one who limps or has a disability in the leg. Listed among those excused from the obligation of striving in Allah's cause.
7.grammar: Definite adjective/noun in the genitive case (majrūr), pattern afʿal (أَفْعَل), masculine singular.
7.root: ع-ر-ج (ʿ-r-j) — to be lame, to limp; aʿraj = lame (one who limps)

8.meaning: Tightness, constriction, or distress of the heart — a sense of being hemmed in, hence unease, difficulty, or the kind of moral discomfort felt when something weighs on one. By extension it can mean blame or sin that constricts the conscience.
8.grammar: The -un ending (nunation) marks an indefinite noun ('a ___ / any ___') in the nominative case, the case typically used for the subject of a sentence or the thing being described as existing.
8.root: ح-ر-ج (ḥ-r-j) — narrowness, constriction, difficulty

9.meaning: 'And not' — a connector 'and' joined to the negative particle 'not,' negating a following statement.
9.grammar: Two particles: the joining 'and' (wa) plus the negator lā ('not'). Lā commonly negates a present-tense verb or a noun. Neither particle takes case endings.

10.meaning: 'To / before / upon' — a preposition whose core sense is being on top of, above, or directed onto something; with a verb of presenting it carries the directional sense 'to / before / in front of,' and it can also convey obligation ('incumbent upon').
10.grammar: A preposition. Its basic meaning is 'on, upon, over,' but with verbs of displaying or presenting it shades into 'to / before / in front of.' It governs the following noun in the genitive case. It is fixed in form and takes no changing ending of its own (its final long -ā is an unchanging part of the word).
10.root: — (preposition; loosely related to the sense of 'height/elevation')

11.meaning: The sick — one who is ill or infirm. Also listed among those excused from fighting in the cause of Allah alongside the blind and lame.
11.grammar: Definite adjective/noun, masculine singular in the genitive case (majrūr).
11.root: م-ر-ض (m-r-ḍ) — to be sick, to be ill; marīḍ = sick person

12.meaning: Tightness, constriction, or distress of the heart — a sense of being hemmed in, hence unease, difficulty, or the kind of moral discomfort felt when something weighs on one. By extension it can mean blame or sin that constricts the conscience.
12.grammar: The -un ending (nunation) marks an indefinite noun ('a ___ / any ___') in the nominative case, the case typically used for the subject of a sentence or the thing being described as existing.

13.meaning: And whoever / and the one who — a joining word plus a relative pronoun introducing a person (or persons) defined by whatever they do; often sets up a condition ('whoever does X …').
13.grammar: A particle 'and' joined to the relative/conditional pronoun man ('whoever, who'). Man does not change its ending; it refers to people and frequently functions as a conditional, so the verb that follows it typically takes the shortened jussive mood.

14.meaning: 'Obeys' / 'complies with' — to follow and carry out the command of another, to be obedient.
14.grammar: A present-tense verb, third person masculine singular ('he obeys'), in the jussive/conditional mood (a mood used after conditional or command particles). The base jussive ends in a silent consonant; the final -i here is a helping vowel added to avoid two unvowelled consonants meeting, not a case ending. The shadda on the yā' is an assimilation (idghām) carried over in recitation from a preceding word.

15.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
15.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

16.meaning: 'And His Messenger' — the one sent with a message, an envoy or apostle, here joined by 'and' and tagged with 'His' (referring to Allah).
16.grammar: Connective 'and' + a masculine noun + the attached pronoun 'his'. The -a ending is accusative, marking the noun as an object of a verb; the suffix -hu ('his') links it in possession to a male referent.

17.meaning: 'He admits him' / 'He causes him to enter' — to bring or cause someone to go into a place. The form is causative: making another enter.
17.grammar: A present-tense causative verb, third person masculine singular ('he makes [someone] enter'), in the jussive/conditional mood (its ending is shortened/unvowelled, the mood used after conditional and command particles). The attached -hu is the object pronoun 'him'.

18.meaning: 'Gardens' — the plural of a lush, walled garden thick with trees whose foliage covers the ground. The root sense is concealment by dense greenery; it is the standard word for the gardens of Paradise.
18.grammar: An indefinite sound feminine plural noun ('gardens'). The '-in' (tanwīn) ending marks it as indefinite ('some gardens'), and for this plural form it stands in the oblique case (genitive or accusative), used after prepositions/possessives or as a direct object.
18.root: ج-ن-ن (j-n-n) — to cover, conceal, hide (hence a dense garden)

19.meaning: A verb 'it flows, runs, streams' — used of water and rivers moving along, and of things that run or course freely. It describes continuous, ongoing motion.
19.grammar: A present/imperfect verb, 3rd person feminine singular. The ta- prefix here marks a feminine 'it/she' subject. The verb describes an ongoing or habitual action: 'it flows / keeps flowing.'

20.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
20.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

21.meaning: 'Beneath it / underneath it' — the noun for the underside or lower region of something, with an attached pronoun 'its' (referring to a feminine thing). It points to the space below or underneath a thing.
21.grammar: A location noun ('underneath') with the attached pronoun '-hā' ('its/her'), referring to a feminine noun. The -i ending is the genitive case, normally triggered here because words of place like 'under' commonly follow a preposition such as 'from' (min taḥti = 'from beneath').

22.meaning: 'The rivers / the streams' — the definite plural of a word for a flowing river or watercourse. It denotes large, running channels of water.
22.grammar: A definite plural noun ('the rivers'). The -u ending is the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence — the doer of the verb or the thing being described.

23.meaning: And whoever / and the one who — a joining word plus a relative pronoun introducing a person (or persons) defined by whatever they do; often sets up a condition ('whoever does X …').
23.grammar: A particle 'and' joined to the relative/conditional pronoun man ('whoever, who'). Man does not change its ending; it refers to people and frequently functions as a conditional, so the verb that follows it typically takes the shortened jussive mood.

24.meaning: "He takes as an ally / turns to in alliance," or simply "turns away," from a verb meaning to turn toward something and befriend/ally with it — or, with the opposite nuance, to turn one's back on it.

parts.en: take as ally / turn to (or away)

24.grammar: The "ya-" prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ("he") in the present-future tense. With the weak final letter dropped (leaving a short "-a"), the verb is in the jussive/subjunctive mood, the form triggered by certain conditional or governing particles. The verb is the reflexive Form V (tafaʿʿala), "to turn oneself toward / take for oneself as ally."
24.root: و-ل-ي (w-l-y) — nearness, alliance; to turn toward, befriend, take charge (or, turn away)

25.meaning: He will punish him — Allah will inflict punishment on the one who turns away. A warning of divine retribution for those who disobey.

parts.en: He punishes / will punish (3rd masc. sg. jussive, Form II)

25.grammar: Imperfect verb in jussive mood (majzūm, marked by sukūn on the final bā'), 3rd person masculine singular, Form II (ʿadhdhaba), with attached 3rd person masculine singular object pronoun.
25.root: ع-ذ-ب (ʿ-dh-b) — to punish; Form II: to punish severely; ʿadhāb = punishment

26.meaning: 'A punishment / torment.' A noun naming chastisement or painful suffering inflicted as a penalty.
26.grammar: A masculine noun. The -an ending marks it as indefinite ('a punishment') and in the accusative case — the form a noun takes as the object of a verb or as the thing being described/quantified.

27.meaning: An adjective meaning 'painful / agonizing'. It describes something that causes intense pain or suffering, whether physical or anguishing.
27.grammar: An adjective in the intensive faʿīl pattern ('intensely ___'). The -an ending is the indefinite accusative ('a painful [one]'), the case typically taken by a noun/adjective serving as an object or agreeing with one.

1.meaning: A two-part emphasis particle meaning 'surely, indeed (already)' — 'la-' strongly affirms, and 'qad' before a past verb stresses that the action has definitely occurred.
1.grammar: Two particles fused for emphasis. 'la-' is the affirming prefix 'surely / truly.' 'qad,' when it precedes a past-tense verb, confirms and intensifies that the action really happened ('has indeed …'). Together they give a strong oath-like assurance to the statement that follows.

2.meaning: To be pleased, well-content, and approving — to accept something with satisfaction and good will. A past-tense verb describing a single subject who became and is pleased: 'he was pleased / he approved.'
2.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb with no prefix. Its bare form with the final -a vowel marks a third-person singular masculine subject ('he'). The perfect tense presents the action as completed: 'was/became pleased, was content.'
2.root: ر-ض-و / ر-ض-ي (r-ḍ-w/y) — to be pleased, content, approving

3.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
3.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.
3.root: — (proper divine name)

4.meaning: About / concerning; a particle marking the topic of inquiry or the thing one moves away from.
4.grammar: A preposition meaning 'about, concerning, away from'. Its base form is ʿan; the final -i here is a helping vowel added to ease pronunciation before a following word beginning with a connecting 'al-'. It governs the genitive case on whatever noun follows.

5.meaning: A plural noun meaning 'the believers' — those who have faith, who inwardly trust and affirm. The Form IV participle denotes one who brings about belief and security within.
5.grammar: A definite plural active participle of Form IV (āmana 'to believe'). The -īna ending marks a sound masculine plural in the accusative/genitive (object or oblique) state. The prefixed mu- marks it as a Form IV participle ('one who has/gives faith').

6.meaning: A particle meaning 'when' or 'at the time that', used to point back to a past moment or event and introduce a recollection of something that occurred.
6.grammar: An indeclinable particle (it has no case ending and never changes form). It signals a point in past time, typically introducing a clause that recalls 'the time when' something happened.

7.meaning: They pledge allegiance to you — they give their hand (bayʿa) to you, entering into a formal covenant of loyalty, obedience, and support. Refers to the Companions swearing allegiance to the Prophet under the tree at Hudaybiyyah (Bayʿat al-Riḍwān).

parts.en: they pledge allegiance (3rd masc. pl. present, Form III)

7.grammar: Imperfect verb, indicative mood, 3rd person masculine plural, Form III (bāyaʿa — reciprocal pledging), with attached 2nd person masculine singular object pronoun. Marked by /-ūna/ suffix.
7.root: ب-ي-ع (b-y-ʿ) — to sell, to exchange; Form III: to pledge allegiance (bayʿa = the pledge/transaction of loyalty)

8.meaning: 'Beneath / underneath.' A location word indicating the space below something.
8.grammar: This is an adverb of place ('under'). It is always in the accusative and characteristically carries the short -a ending; it normally attaches to a following noun, giving the sense 'beneath …'.
8.root: ت-ح-ت (t-ḥ-t) — lowness, that which is below

9.meaning: 'The tree' — a singular noun for a tree or, more broadly, any woody plant or shrub. The -at ending gives it the single-item form drawn from the collective for trees/vegetation.
9.grammar: A noun with the definite article al- ('the'); its l sound assimilates into the following sh. The -a(t) ending is the 'unit' marker that singles out one item ('a/the [single] tree') from the collective 'trees.' The final -i is genitive, the case used after a preposition or in a possessive 'of' link.
9.root: ش-ج-ر (sh-j-r) — tree, vegetation; to grow/branch out

10.meaning: And He knew — past tense: Allah perceived and knew something (specifically, what was in the hearts of the believers at Hudaybiyyah). Divine knowledge preceding and encompassing all events.
10.grammar: Consecutive fa + past tense verb, 3rd person masculine singular, Form I (ʿalima — to know).

11.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
11.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

12.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
12.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

13.meaning: 'Their hearts' — the plural of qalb ('heart'), joined to the pronoun 'their'. In Qur'anic usage the 'heart' (qalb) is the seat of understanding, intention, faith, and feeling, not merely the physical organ.
13.grammar: Qulūb is the broken (irregular) plural of qalb, 'hearts'. The -i ending is genitive: here it appears because the noun follows a preposition and because it is possessed by an attached pronoun. The suffix -him means 'their' (a masculine plural group), and its -i- vowel matches the preceding genitive ending. So the whole means 'hearts belonging to them'.
13.root: ق-ل-ب (q-l-b) — heart; to turn over, turn about, change

14.meaning: A verb meaning 'and/then he sent down / caused to descend,' the act of bringing something down from a higher place (often used of revelation, rain, or aid descending from Allah).
14.grammar: A perfect (past-tense) verb of the causative (Form IV) pattern 'anzala,' 3rd person masculine singular, prefixed with the connector fa- ('so/then'). The a- prefix turns 'to descend' into 'to send/bring down.' The final -a marks 'he' as the doer of a completed action: 'so He sent down.'

15.meaning: The tranquility, the peace of heart — a special inner calm and reassurance sent by Allah upon the believers' hearts in times of fear or stress. A spiritual state of steadfast serenity.

parts.en: the tranquility / the peace of heart (definite accusative)

15.grammar: Definite feminine noun with the definite article al-, in the accusative case (manṣūb) marked by the -a ending (fatḥa). Serves as the direct object of the verb anzala (He sent down).
15.root: س-ك-ن (s-k-n) — to dwell, to be still, to find peace; sakinah = divine tranquility

16.meaning: A compound meaning 'upon them' or 'against them': the preposition ʿalā ('on, upon, over, against') joined to the plural pronoun 'them'. It conveys something resting on, being incumbent upon, or weighing against a group.
16.grammar: ʿalā shifts to the form ʿalay- before a pronoun. The suffix -him is the attached pronominal suffix for a masculine plural group ('them'); after a preposition it carries genitive/prepositional force, and the -i- vowel reflects its position after this preposition. Together they signal a relationship of something being over, upon, or burdensome to that group.
16.root: — (preposition with attached pronoun; no triliteral root)

17.meaning: And He rewarded them — Allah bestowed upon them a reward (the reward of the conquest of Makkah and divine pleasure). Past tense expressing a completed divine act.

parts.en: He rewarded (3rd masc. sg. past, Form IV)

17.grammar: Conjunction wāw + past tense verb, 3rd person masculine singular, Form IV (athāba — to reward, to recompense), with attached 3rd person masculine plural object pronoun.
17.root: ث-و-ب (th-w-b) — to return; Form IV: to reward; thawāb = reward

18.meaning: A clear, manifest opening or victory — a decisive triumph that removes an obstacle and opens the way forward. In Qur'anic usage it denotes a victory granted by Allah that unfolds with clarity and completeness.
18.grammar: Indefinite masculine noun in the accusative case (manṣūb), marked by tanwīn fatḥ (-an). Serves as the object of the implied verb or predicate complement.
18.root: ف-ت-ح (f-t-ḥ) — to open, to conquer, to grant victory

19.meaning: An adjective meaning 'near, close, close at hand' — describing something short in distance, time, or relationship, easily reached or soon to come.
19.grammar: A masculine singular adjective on the 'faʿīl' pattern ('near, close'). The ending -an is the accusative case with tanwīn (nunation), which typically marks the word as agreeing with an accusative noun it describes, or otherwise governed into the accusative; the tanwīn shows it is indefinite.

1.meaning: And spoils of war — additional war-booty gained alongside the near victory. References the bounty Allah promised to the believers at Hudaybiyyah.

parts.en: spoils of war (indefinite plural accusative, diptote)

1.grammar: Conjunction wāw + broken plural of maghnam, accusative case, diptote (no tanwīn).
1.root: غ-ن-م (gh-n-m) — to profit, to gain; maghānim = war spoils

2.meaning: Much / many / great in quantity — an adjective indicating abundance. Describes the spoils of war as being plentiful and the favour of Allah as great.
2.grammar: Indefinite feminine adjective in the accusative case (manṣūb), marked by tanwīn fatḥ with tā' marbūṭa.
2.root: ك-ث-ر (k-th-r) — to be much, to be many; kathīr = many, much; kathīra (f) = much/many (feminine)

3.meaning: That they will take / seize — referring to the believers who will receive and take those spoils. The relative clause describes the promised war-booty.

parts.en: they will take (3rd masc. pl. imperfect indicative)

3.grammar: Imperfect verb, indicative mood, 3rd person masculine plural, Form I (akhadha — to take), with attached 3rd person feminine singular object pronoun (referring to maghānim).
3.root: أ-خ-ذ (ʾ-kh-dh) — to take, to seize, to receive

4.meaning: And he was / he became — a verb of being that places a subject in a past state or links it to a description in the past.
4.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'kāna' is a past-tense verb, 3rd-person masculine singular, meaning 'he was/became'; it commonly introduces a past condition and is typically followed by a noun describing the subject's state. The final -a marks completed past action by a single male.
4.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existence

5.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
5.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

6.meaning: Mighty, all-powerful, invincible — one who is dominant and cannot be overcome; also carrying the sense of precious and held in high honor. Of a person it means strong and unassailable.
6.grammar: An intensive adjective (of the faʿīl pattern, conveying a deep, settled quality). The final -an (tanwīn fatḥ) marks it as indefinite and in the accusative case, which typically signals a direct object or a descriptive complement governed into the accusative.
6.root: ع-ز-ز (ʿ-z-z) — might, strength, dominance; also honor and preciousness

7.meaning: All-Wise; one possessing perfect wisdom, who places everything in its right place and decides with flawless judgement. As an intensive form it conveys wisdom that is complete and sound.
7.grammar: An intensive adjective ('all-wise') on the faʿīl pattern, stressing the quality to its fullest degree. The -an (tanwīn) combines the -a accusative ending — typical of a predicate or object — with the -n marking it indefinite.
7.root: ح-ك-م (ḥ-k-m) — wisdom, sound judgement, governance

1.meaning: Allah has promised you (plural) — a statement of divine promise made to the community. Allah's promise here is for the conquest of Khaybar and further victories.

parts.en: promised (3rd masc. sg. past, Form I)
you (2nd masc. pl. object pronoun with liaison vowel)

1.grammar: Past tense verb, 3rd person masculine singular, Form I (waʿada — to promise), with attached 2nd person masculine plural object pronoun -kumu.
