So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.
2.root: — (proper divine name)

3.meaning: Spoils of war, war-booty — the goods and wealth captured from the enemy after a battle. Plural of maghnam. In the context of 48:15, the Bedouin who stayed behind hope to take the spoils of Khaybar.

parts.en: spoils of war / booty (indefinite plural accusative, diptote)

3.grammar: Broken plural of maghnam (مَغْنَم), in the accusative case (manṣūb), diptote (no tanwīn).
3.root: غ-ن-م (gh-n-m) — to gain, to profit; ghaniīma/maghnam = war-booty, spoils; ghunm = gain

4.meaning: Much / many / great in quantity — an adjective indicating abundance. Describes the spoils of war as being plentiful and the favour of Allah as great.
4.grammar: Indefinite feminine adjective in the accusative case (manṣūb), marked by tanwīn fatḥ with tā' marbūṭa.
4.root: ك-ث-ر (k-th-r) — to be much, to be many; kathīr = many, much; kathīra (f) = much/many (feminine)

5.meaning: That you (plural) will take it — that you will receive and take the spoils. Referring to the believers taking the booty that Allah has promised them.

parts.en: you (pl.) will take (2nd masc. pl. imperfect indicative)

5.grammar: Imperfect verb, indicative mood, 2nd person masculine plural, Form I (akhadha), with attached 3rd person feminine singular object pronoun.

6.meaning: And He hastened / and He caused to come quickly — Allah expedited something (this near victory / Khaybar spoils) for them ahead of the originally scheduled time.

parts.en: He hastened / hurried (3rd masc. sg. past, Form II)

6.grammar: Consecutive fa + past tense verb, 3rd person masculine singular, Form II (ʿajjala — to hasten, to expedite).
6.root: ع-ج-ل (ʿ-j-l) — to be quick, to hurry; Form II: to hasten, to expedite; ʿajala = haste

7.meaning: 'For you' or 'to you' — the preposition of benefit or attribution ('for / belonging to') combined with a plural 'you', marking the people for whose benefit or possession something is done.
7.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The prefix la- (the preposition li- 'for', here vowelled 'la' before a pronoun) conveys benefit, purpose, or belonging. The suffix -kum is the second-person masculine plural object, 'you all'.

8.meaning: Feminine singular demonstrative pronoun, 'this (one)' — pointing to a single nearby thing that is grammatically feminine.
8.grammar: A demonstrative ('this') for a single feminine thing close at hand, contrasting with the masculine 'hādhā.' Demonstratives in Arabic do not change for grammatical case; the form stays fixed whether subject, object, or after a preposition.
8.root: — (demonstrative pronoun; no triliteral root)

9.meaning: And He withheld / and He restrained — Allah held back something (the hands of the enemies) from harming the believers, protecting them.

parts.en: He withheld / restrained (3rd masc. sg. past, Form I)

9.grammar: Conjunction wāw + past tense verb, 3rd person masculine singular, Form I (kaffa — to restrain, to hold back). Doubled root.
9.root: ك-ف-ف (k-f-f) — to restrain, to hold back, to refrain; kaff = palm of the hand (what holds back)

10.meaning: The hands of — plural of yad (hand). Here it refers to the hands of the enemies being held back by Allah from fighting the believers during the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah.
10.grammar: Broken plural of yad (يَد), in the accusative case (manṣūb) in construct (iḍāfa) with the following noun (the enemy).
10.root: ي-د-ي (y-d-y) — hand; aydin/aydī = hands (irregular plural of yad)

11.meaning: Humankind, people, mankind — the collective of human beings.
11.grammar: A collective noun ('people, mankind') carrying the definite article al- ('the'); the 'l' of the article assimilates into the following 'n', doubling it (al-nās → an-nās). The genitive ending -i marks the word as governed by a preposition or as the second term of a possessive.
11.root: ء-ن-س (ʾ-n-s) — humankind, sociability, familiarity; the word for 'people' is most commonly traced to this root (related to insān, 'human being')

12.meaning: 'From you / off you' (addressing a group). The preposition 'ʿan' (denoting moving away from, or 'concerning') fused with a plural 'you'.
12.grammar: A preposition 'ʿan' with an attached pronoun object. 'ʿan' conveys moving away or off from something (and so pairs naturally with pardoning — lifting a fault away); the suffix '-kum' means a plural 'you'.

13.meaning: And so that it may be — introducing a purpose clause: so that this act of divine restraint serves an additional purpose (to be a sign, or for the knowledge of the believers to be evident).

parts.en: it may be (3rd fem. sg. subjunctive of kāna)

13.grammar: Conjunction wāw + lām of purpose + imperfect verb in subjunctive mood, 3rd person feminine singular of kāna (to be), in the subjunctive.
13.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist; kāna = was/were (auxiliary)

14.meaning: 'A sign' — a token, mark, or proof that points to something beyond itself; a miraculous indication, a lesson, or an evidence. (The same word also denotes a verse of the Qur'an.)
14.grammar: An indefinite noun. The '-an' ending (accusative with 'tanwīn', the doubled final 'n' of indefiniteness) typically marks the noun as the direct object of a verb, or as the thing one is being made or named, and signals 'a / an' rather than 'the'.

15.meaning: 'For the believers' — for those who have faith: those who trust, affirm, and feel secure in their belief in Allah and what He has revealed.
15.grammar: A masculine sound plural active participle ('believers') with the -īna ending, here the genitive/oblique form required after the preposition li- ('for, to'). With the article, li- + al- contracts to lil-.
15.root: أ-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — safety, security, trust; (form IV) to believe, to have faith

16.meaning: 'And to guide you' — and that He may lead you on the right way, directing a group along the path of right guidance.

parts.en: guides / leads on the right way (present-tense stem)

16.grammar: Connector wa ('and') + a present-tense verb, 3rd-person masculine singular 'He guides', + the object 'you' (a group of males). The ya- prefix signals 'he'. The -a ending on the verb (-hdiya) is the subjunctive, carried over from a preceding 'so that' purpose; it gives the sense 'and that He may guide'. The suffix -kum is the one guided.
16.root: ه-د-ي (h-d-y) — guidance, to lead rightly, to show the way

17.meaning: 'A path', 'a way', 'a road' — a clear route or way that one travels, often used for a course of conduct or a way of life.
17.grammar: A noun. The '-an' ending is the indefinite accusative with nunation ('a path', not 'the path'); the accusative typically marks the direct object of a verb.

18.meaning: 'Straight', 'upright', 'level' — describes something direct and without crookedness or deviation; figuratively, correct and sound.
18.grammar: An active participle (a 'doer'-form describing a state) on the 'mustafʿil' pattern, literally 'that which holds itself straight'. The '-an' ending is the indefinite accusative with nunation, agreeing with the indefinite accusative noun it describes.
18.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — standing, being upright; here, being straight

1.meaning: And others — additional (things, victories, or people) beyond what has been mentioned. Refers to other future bounties or victories Allah has in store for the believers.

parts.en: others / another (feminine singular or plural, oblique)

1.grammar: Conjunction wāw + feminine adjective/pronoun of ukhar (آخَر/أُخَر — other), in the accusative or nominative as ḥāl or ʿaṭf.
1.root: أ-خ-ر (ʾ-kh-r) — to be last, to come after; ākhir = other, another, later

2.meaning: A negating particle, 'not', used specifically to deny that an action happened in the past, even though it attaches to a present-tense verb form. It turns 'you do X' into 'you did not do X'.

parts.en: did not (negation of a completed act)

2.grammar: An indeclinable particle that governs the verb after it, putting that verb into the jussive (clipped) mood and giving it past-time meaning. In short: lam + a present-form verb = 'did not [verb]'.
2.root: — (particle; no triliteral root)

3.meaning: "you (all) have power over, are able to overpower, gain mastery over" — a verb of having capacity, control, or the upper hand.
3.grammar: A present-tense verb, second-person masculine plural ("you all"), in the subjunctive/jussive mood. The "ta-" prefix marks "you"; the plural ending's final "-na" is dropped to "-ū," which signals the subjunctive/jussive — used after certain particles or in conditional/purpose clauses.
3.root: ق-د-ر (q-d-r) — power, ability, measure, decree

4.meaning: 'On it / upon it / over it' — the preposition 'alā ('on, upon, against') joined to the pronoun 'it/her', referring to a single feminine or grammatically feminine thing.
4.grammar: 'ʿalā' is a preposition meaning 'on/upon/over'; its ending shifts to -ay when a pronoun is attached. The suffix -hā is the object pronoun for a single feminine (or feminine-gender) thing. Together they mean 'on it'. Words after a preposition stand in the genitive, though attached pronouns like -hā do not visibly change form.

5.meaning: A short particle placed before a verb to emphasize or affirm it. Before a past-tense verb it means 'indeed / certainly / has already (happened)'; before a present-tense verb it can mean 'sometimes / may'. It sharpens and confirms the verb that follows.
5.grammar: An indeclinable particle (its form never changes). It does not take case or tense endings; its job is to color the following verb — affirming and intensifying a past action ('has indeed done') or signaling occasional possibility with a present verb.

6.meaning: He encompassed, surrounded, or enclosed completely — to take in fully on every side, whether physically surrounding something or having total knowledge/grasp of it.
6.grammar: A past-tense (completed-action) verb in the third-person masculine singular ('he'). It is a Form IV verb (the pattern aFʿaLa, marked by the prefixed hamza 'a-'), which typically makes a root transitive or causative — here, to bring something wholly within one's encompassing. The final -a is the standard vowel closing a past-tense verb of this person.
6.root: ح-و-ط (ḥ-w-ṭ) — to surround, encompass, guard

8.meaning: with it / by it — a preposition meaning 'with' or 'by means of' joined to a pronoun referring to a single feminine (or grammatically feminine) thing.
8.grammar: The bi- prefix is a preposition meaning 'with', 'by', or 'by means of'. The attached -hā is an object pronoun meaning 'it' or 'her', referring to something feminine in gender. Together they mean 'with it' or 'by means of it'.

11.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
11.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

12.meaning: 'every,' 'each,' or 'all' — a word expressing totality or completeness. It indicates the entirety of something: when joined to a singular indefinite noun it means 'every (single) one,' and when joined to a definite noun it can mean 'all of' or 'the whole of.'
12.grammar: A noun of totality. The final '-i' ending is genitive (the 'of/possession' case): it marks the word as governed by a preceding preposition or as the first term of a possessive link to a following noun, so it typically reads 'of every…' or 'every…' leading into what follows.

13.meaning: 'a thing' — anything that exists or can be conceived, an entity or matter in the most general sense. It is the broadest Arabic word for 'something,' covering objects, affairs, and abstractions alike.
13.grammar: An indefinite singular noun. The '-in' ending (tanwīn al-kasr) signals two things at once: indefiniteness ('a thing,' not 'the thing') and the genitive case, marking it as following a preposition or completing a possessive link to a preceding noun.
13.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʼ) — to will, to be a thing/existent

14.meaning: An adjective meaning 'all-powerful,' 'fully capable,' 'one who has complete power to do anything.' As a divine attribute it denotes Allah's absolute and unrestricted ability over all things.
14.grammar: An intensive adjective ('most capable, all-powerful'). The -an ending is the accusative with indefinite (tanwīn) marking, typically used as the predicate of a 'was/is' statement or as an object; the doubled-n sound shows indefiniteness.

1.meaning: 'and if' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the particle 'if'. This particular 'if' (law) introduces a hypothetical or contrary-to-fact condition: 'if (such-and-such had been the case)…', often implying it was not.
1.grammar: A conjunction plus a conditional particle. wa- means 'and'. law is a non-changing particle (no case ending) that sets up a supposition, typically answered by a clause beginning with la- ('… then certainly …').

2.meaning: They fight you (plural) — they will engage you in battle, go to war against you. Refers to the promised enemy that the believers will encounter.

parts.en: they fight / fought you (pl.) (3rd masc. pl. past/conditional, Form III)

2.grammar: Past tense verb used in a conditional context, 3rd person masculine plural, Form III (qātala — reciprocal fighting), with attached 2nd person masculine plural object pronoun -kumu.
2.root: ق-ت-ل (q-t-l) — to kill; Form III: to fight against (qitāl = combat)

3.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
3.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

4.meaning: 'They disbelieved / rejected faith' — from a root meaning to cover over or conceal. To disbelieve in this sense is to cover up and refuse the truth, and also to be ungrateful, hiding or denying favours received.
4.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third person masculine plural: 'they disbelieved'. The completed action is built into the stem kafara ('he disbelieved'), and the -ū suffix (written وا) marks the doer as 'they' (masculine plural). The silent alif written after the -ū is a spelling convention with no sound.
4.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; to reject faith, be ungrateful

5.meaning: They would have turned away / they surely would have fled — a counterfactual statement: had the encounter taken place, the enemies would have turned their backs and fled.

parts.en: surely (lām of emphasis / response to law)
they turned away / fled (3rd masc. pl. past, Form II)

5.grammar: Lām of the jawāb al-law (response particle) + past tense verb, 3rd person masculine plural, Form II (wallā — to turn away, to flee, to put something at the back).
5.root: و-ل-ي (w-l-y) — to be near, to take charge; Form II: to turn away (wallā = he turned his back)

6.meaning: The backs — the plural of 'back', the rear of the body. Turning one's 'backs' is a common image for fleeing or retreating.
6.grammar: A definite plural noun ('the backs'). The al- prefix means 'the'. The -a ending is accusative, the case that commonly marks the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon). The form adbār is a broken (irregular internal) plural of the singular dubur, 'back / hindpart'.
6.root: د-ب-ر (d-b-r) — the back, rear, hind part; that which comes behind

7.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'then' or 'thereafter' that links two statements in sequence, but unlike a simple 'and' it signals an ordered succession with a sense of delay or interval — one thing happens, and after some lapse the next follows.
7.grammar: An invariable connective particle; it has no case ending and never changes form. Its function is to coordinate clauses in temporal or logical order, implying that what follows comes after a gap or interval.

8.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
8.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

9.meaning: 'they find' — to come upon, obtain, or encounter something; to perceive a thing to be present or available.
9.grammar: A present/future verb, 3rd-person masculine plural ('they …'). The ending -ūna combines the plural 'they' (-ū) with the indicative marker -na, signalling a simple ongoing or future statement (not negated or subjunctive). The ya- prefix marks the third person.
9.root: و-ج-د (w-j-d) — to find, come upon, obtain

10.meaning: A guardian, protector, ally, or close supporter — one who is near and takes charge of another's affairs. Waliyy carries the sense of nearness combined with care, authority, and friendship.
10.grammar: An indefinite noun ('a protector'). The -an ending (tanwīn fatḥa) is the accusative case: it commonly marks the word as a direct object of a verb, or as a predicate/complement after certain verbs of 'making' or 'becoming'.

11.meaning: 'And not' — a connector 'and' joined to the negative particle 'not,' negating a following statement.
11.grammar: Two particles: the joining 'and' (wa) plus the negator lā ('not'). Lā commonly negates a present-tense verb or a noun. Neither particle takes case endings.

12.meaning: 'A helper, supporter, one who gives aid and victory' — an intensive form stressing reliable, effective help.
12.grammar: An indefinite noun on an intensive pattern (faʿīl) that conveys a strong or constant doer — 'a true helper'. The -an ending marks the accusative and indefiniteness, commonly used here as a specifier naming the capacity ('as a helper').
12.root: ن-ص-ر (n-ṣ-r) — to help, to aid, to give victory

1.meaning: An established way, practice, or norm; a consistent pattern of conduct that is followed as a precedent. When ascribed to Allah it denotes His unchanging way of dealing with creation.
1.grammar: A noun in the accusative case, marked by the final -a (often an object, or set as an emphatic statement). As the first term of a possessive pairing it links to a following noun, meaning 'the way of …'.
1.root: س-ن-ن (s-n-n) — to set a precedent; an established way

2.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
2.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

3.meaning: A feminine singular relative pronoun: 'the one which / that which / who' (referring to a single feminine thing). It introduces a descriptive clause that tells us more about a preceding feminine noun.
3.grammar: A relative pronoun, feminine singular, fixed in form (it does not change for case). It links a feminine noun to a following clause describing it, the equivalent of English 'which,' 'that,' or 'who.'

4.meaning: A short particle placed before a verb to emphasize or affirm it. Before a past-tense verb it means 'indeed / certainly / has already (happened)'; before a present-tense verb it can mean 'sometimes / may'. It sharpens and confirms the verb that follows.
4.grammar: An indeclinable particle (its form never changes). It does not take case or tense endings; its job is to color the following verb — affirming and intensifying a past action ('has indeed done') or signaling occasional possibility with a present verb.
4.root: — (no triliteral root; an emphasizing particle)

5.meaning: 'It passed away / went by, came to an end' — said of a community, time, or era that has elapsed and is now gone. The root carries the sense of being emptied out, hence of time or people that have passed.
5.grammar: Past-tense verb. The -t (sukūn-marked -at) suffix marks a third-person feminine singular subject, 'she/it,' used here because the noun it refers to is grammatically feminine. The past tense states a completed action.
5.root: خ-ل-و (kh-l-w) — to be empty/vacant; to pass away, elapse

6.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
6.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.
6.root: — (preposition)

7.meaning: An adverb of time meaning 'before / beforehand / previously,' pointing to a moment or state that precedes something else in time. When used with the final vowel -u (qablu), it stands cut off from an explicit following noun, conveying 'before(hand)' or 'previously' in an absolute sense — the thing it is 'before' is understood rather than stated.
7.grammar: An adverb of time. The final -u ending here is the indeclinable (mabnī) form taken when the word is severed from a following genitive: rather than 'before X,' it means 'before(hand)' on its own, with the reference point left implicit.
7.root: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l) — to come before, precede, be in front; to receive/accept

8.meaning: A two-part expression combining 'and' with the particle of emphatic future negation. The core particle 'lan' negates a coming action with finality: 'will never / shall not (ever).' It denies that something will happen in the future, often with a tone of absolute impossibility.
8.grammar: A conjunction 'wa' ('and') joined to the negating particle 'lan'. 'Lan' governs a following present-tense verb, putting it into the subjunctive mood and turning its meaning into an emphatic denial of the future: 'it will never happen.'

9.meaning: A second-person present verb: 'you find / you come upon.' It denotes discovering or encountering something, whether by searching or by chance.
9.grammar: The ta- prefix marks a second-person masculine singular subject ('you'). The final -a vowel is the subjunctive, the shape used after governing particles (such as 'never' or 'that'), often projecting the action into the future.
9.root: و-ج-د (w-j-d) — to find, to come upon

10.meaning: In the way/custom of Allah — sunnatu Allāh: the established and unchanging pattern, way, or practice of Allah in dealing with creation, particularly in rewarding the faithful and punishing the disobedient.
10.grammar: Preposition lām + feminine noun sunnah in the genitive case (majrūr) in construct (iḍāfa).
10.root: س-ن-ن (s-n-n) — to establish a path/custom; sunnah = established way, custom, practice

11.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
11.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

12.meaning: Any change / any alteration — referring to the impossibility of finding any change in Allah's established way (sunnah). Allah's patterns and laws do not change.

parts.en: any change / alteration (indefinite masculine accusative, verbal noun Form II)

12.grammar: Indefinite verbal noun (maṣdar) of Form II (baddala — to change), in the accusative case, marked by tanwīn fatḥ (-an).
12.root: ب-د-ل (b-d-l) — to change, to exchange; tabdīl = changing, alteration (Form II maṣdar)

1.meaning: 'And He' — the connective 'and' joined to the standalone pronoun 'He' (a single masculine person or thing), often introducing a new clause about the same subject.
1.grammar: A connective particle plus an independent pronoun. The wa- prefix means 'and', joining clauses or words. 'Huwa' is the detached third-person masculine singular pronoun; it carries no case ending, its final -a being fixed.

2.meaning: A relative pronoun meaning 'the one who' or 'which' — it points back to a masculine singular person or thing and introduces a clause that describes or identifies it. It works like the English 'who/which/that' that opens a defining clause.
2.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) masculine singular relative pronoun: its form does not change for case, so the ending stays -ī whatever grammatical role it fills. It always needs a following clause to complete its meaning.

3.meaning: He withheld / restrained — same root as the earlier entry but here standing alone without the conjunction, expressing Allah's act of restraining the unbelievers' hands at Makkah.

parts.en: He withheld / restrained (3rd masc. sg. past, Form I)

3.grammar: Past tense verb, 3rd person masculine singular, Form I (kaffa). Doubled root ك-ف-ف.
3.root: ك-ف-ف (k-f-f) — to restrain, to hold back; kaff = the palm (that holds back)

4.meaning: Their hands — the physical hands; often figuratively the means by which one acts, strikes, or exerts force (plural of 'hand').
4.grammar: A plural noun (aydī, plural of yad, 'hand') with the attached possessive -hum ('their'). The -a vowel before the pronoun marks the accusative case, which typically signals that the word is the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon).
4.root: ي-د-ي (y-d-y) — hand

5.meaning: 'From you / off you' (addressing a group). The preposition 'ʿan' (denoting moving away from, or 'concerning') fused with a plural 'you'.
5.grammar: A preposition 'ʿan' with an attached pronoun object. 'ʿan' conveys moving away or off from something (and so pairs naturally with pardoning — lifting a fault away); the suffix '-kum' means a plural 'you'.

6.meaning: A noun phrase meaning 'and your hands'. 'Yad' is the hand (and by extension power or agency); here it appears in its plural form with an attached possessive.
6.grammar: A plural noun joined by 'wa-' ('and') and carrying the possessive ending -kum ('your', for a group). The -a vowel before the suffix reflects the accusative/object case, typically marking the noun as the thing acted upon.
6.root: ي-د-ي (y-d-y) — hand

7.meaning: From them; away from them; concerning them. The preposition ʿan conveys moving away from, departing from, or 'on behalf of / concerning', combined with the pronoun 'them'.
7.grammar: A preposition joined to the attached pronoun -hum, 'them' (referring to a group, grammatically masculine plural). The preposition ʿan basically signals separation or removal ('away from'), and can also mean 'about/concerning' or 'on behalf of' depending on usage.
7.root: — (a preposition; no triliteral verbal root)

8.meaning: Within / in the belly of — a prepositional phrase indicating location inside something. Here, bibaṭni Makkata = within (the environs of) Makkah, referring to Hudaybiyyah which is near Makkah.
8.grammar: Preposition bā' + masculine noun baṭn in the genitive case in construct (iḍāfa) with the following noun (Makkata).
8.root: ب-ط-ن (b-ṭ-n) — belly, interior, inside; bibaṭni = inside / within

9.meaning: Makkah — the holy city in the Arabian Peninsula, the site of the Kaʿba and the direction of prayer (qibla). Here it refers to the location near which the events of Hudaybiyyah took place.
9.grammar: Proper noun (diptote: no tanwīn), in the genitive case (majrūr) as the second element of the iḍāfa (baṭni Makkata).
9.root: — (proper noun; no trilateral root derivation)

10.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
10.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

11.meaning: A noun/adverb meaning 'after' — the time or position following something; 'afterward', 'following'.
11.grammar: An adverb of time functioning as a noun, here in the genitive case marked by the final -i. The genitive ending typically appears after a preposition or as the second term of a construct ('after THE …'), linking 'after' to a following noun to specify what it comes after.
11.root: ب-ع-د (b-ʿ-d) — to be after, to follow, distance in place or time

12.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
12.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

13.meaning: He gave you victory over them / He made you overcome them — Allah granted the believers superiority and victory over their enemies at the conquest of Makkah.

parts.en: He gave victory / made to triumph (3rd masc. sg. past, Form IV)

13.grammar: Past tense verb, 3rd person masculine singular, Form IV (aẓfara — to grant victory over), with attached 2nd person masculine plural object pronoun.
13.root: ظ-ف-ر (ẓ-f-r) — to be victorious, to triumph; Form IV: to give victory; ẓafar = victory, triumph

14.meaning: A compound meaning 'upon them' or 'against them': the preposition ʿalā ('on, upon, over, against') joined to the plural pronoun 'them'. It conveys something resting on, being incumbent upon, or weighing against a group.
14.grammar: ʿalā shifts to the form ʿalay- before a pronoun. The suffix -him is the attached pronominal suffix for a masculine plural group ('them'); after a preposition it carries genitive/prepositional force, and the -i- vowel reflects its position after this preposition. Together they signal a relationship of something being over, upon, or burdensome to that group.
14.root: — (preposition with attached pronoun; no triliteral root)

15.meaning: And he was / he became — a verb of being that places a subject in a past state or links it to a description in the past.
15.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'kāna' is a past-tense verb, 3rd-person masculine singular, meaning 'he was/became'; it commonly introduces a past condition and is typically followed by a noun describing the subject's state. The final -a marks completed past action by a single male.

16.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
16.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

17.meaning: A phrase meaning 'in/with that which' or 'in what' — combining the sense of 'by means of' or 'concerning' with an unspecified thing ('whatever it may be').
17.grammar: The preposition bi ('in, with, by means of, concerning') attached to the relative/indefinite pronoun mā ('what, that which'). Both elements are invariable, so the phrase carries no case ending. A word governed by the preposition bi is understood to be in the genitive relationship.

18.meaning: You (all) do / work / act — to carry out deeds or labor.
18.grammar: A present-tense verb (Form I). The 'ta-' prefix with the '-ūna' ending marks the second-person masculine plural ('you all'). The '-ūna' (with final 'n') is the indicative form, marking a plain ongoing or habitual statement.
18.root: ع-م-ل (ʿ-m-l) — to do, work, act; deeds

19.meaning: All-Seeing — one who sees fully and perfectly. An intensive adjective (faʿīl pattern) expressing sight as a permanent, comprehensive attribute that misses nothing.
19.grammar: An indefinite noun/adjective on the intensive faʿīl pattern. The final -an (tanwīn fatḥah) marks the accusative case — the form used for the object of a verb or a predicate after certain particles — and the -n shows it is indefinite ('a seer / seeing').

1.meaning: An independent (standalone) pronoun meaning 'they' (masculine plural). Standing on its own, it typically adds emphasis or marks the group out as the focus ('they, specifically', 'it is they who').
1.grammar: A detached subject pronoun, third person masculine plural. It takes no case endings; the base is hum, and the final vowel appears as -u (humu) as a connecting vowel to ease pronunciation before a following word beginning with a definite article. Standing alone, it commonly emphasises or isolates the subject.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: 'They disbelieved / rejected faith' — from a root meaning to cover over or conceal. To disbelieve in this sense is to cover up and refuse the truth, and also to be ungrateful, hiding or denying favours received.
3.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third person masculine plural: 'they disbelieved'. The completed action is built into the stem kafara ('he disbelieved'), and the -ū suffix (written وا) marks the doer as 'they' (masculine plural). The silent alif written after the -ū is a spelling convention with no sound.
3.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; to reject faith, be ungrateful

4.meaning: And they hindered you / barred you — referring to the polytheists preventing the Prophet and believers from entering Makkah to perform ʿUmra. Part of the context of the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah.

parts.en: they barred / hindered (3rd masc. pl. past, Form I)

4.grammar: Conjunction wāw + past tense verb, 3rd person masculine plural, Form I (ṣadda — to block, to prevent), with attached 2nd person masculine plural object pronoun. Doubled root.
4.root: ص-د-د (ṣ-d-d) — to block, to bar, to turn away; ṣadd = obstruction, barrier

5.meaning: About / concerning; a particle marking the topic of inquiry or the thing one moves away from.
5.grammar: A preposition meaning 'about, concerning, away from'. Its base form is ʿan; the final -i here is a helping vowel added to ease pronunciation before a following word beginning with a connecting 'al-'. It governs the genitive case on whatever noun follows.

6.meaning: The place of prostration; a mosque — literally the spot where one bows down (sajda) in worship. With the following 'sacred', it names the Sacred Mosque.
6.grammar: A noun of place on the form mafʿil ('the place where prostration is done'), prefixed with al- ('the'). The final -i ending is the genitive case, which typically marks the word as following a preposition or as the possessed/qualified noun after another ('… OF the mosque').
6.root: س-ج-د (s-j-d) — prostration, bowing down in worship

7.meaning: The sacred, inviolable, forbidden; that which is set apart and protected, whose violation is prohibited out of reverence. Describes something hallowed.
7.grammar: An adjective on the form faʿāl ('sacred/forbidden'), prefixed with al- ('the'). The final -i ending is the genitive case; an adjective takes the same case as the noun it describes, so this -i matches a preceding genitive noun ('the … sacred').
7.root: ح-ر-م (ḥ-r-m) — being forbidden, sacred, set apart, inviolable

8.meaning: And the sacrificial offering — the animal dedicated and led to be slaughtered as a devotional gift at a sacred place.
8.grammar: A definite noun with the article al- ('the'), preceded by the connector wa- ('and'). The -a ending marks the accusative case, the form a noun takes as a direct object of a verb.
8.root: ه-د-ي (h-d-y) — to guide, lead; to present a gift

9.meaning: Detained / prevented / confined — a passive participle; the sacrificial animals were prevented from reaching their destination (the Kaʿba), kept back and unable to proceed.

parts.en: detained / confined / prevented (indefinite masculine accusative passive participle)

9.grammar: Indefinite passive participle (mafʿūl), Form I (ʿakafa — to confine, to be kept in one place), masculine singular in the accusative case as ḥāl (circumstantial).
9.root: ع-ك-ف (ʿ-k-f) — to stay at, to confine oneself to a place; maʿkūf = detained, kept back

10.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
10.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

11.meaning: Reaching / arriving at — a verb in the subjunctive expressing purpose or condition: the sacrificial animals reaching their destined place of slaughter (the Kaʿba area).

parts.en: it reaches / arrives at (3rd masc. sg. subjunctive, Form I)

11.grammar: Imperfect verb in the subjunctive mood, 3rd person masculine singular, Form I (balagha — to reach, to arrive at). -a ending marks subjunctive.
11.root: ب-ل-غ (b-l-gh) — to reach, to arrive at, to attain; bulūgh = reaching, attainment

12.meaning: Its lawful place or appointed destination — the point at which something reaches the spot where the act concerning it (such as sacrifice) becomes permissible.
12.grammar: A place-noun (a noun of location formed on the ma- pattern) with an attached possessive pronoun. The -a is the accusative ending, often marking a destination or the object of a verb. The suffix -hu means 'its' or 'his'.
12.root: ح-ل-ل (ḥ-l-l) — to alight/settle, to untie, to become lawful/permitted

13.meaning: "and were it not for / and if not for" — a compound particle introducing a hypothetical: it points to something whose existence prevents a stated consequence, i.e. 'had it not been for X, then Y would have happened'.

parts.en: were it not for / if not

13.grammar: A particle phrase, not a verb, so it carries no case or tense ending. It sets up a conditional that is contrary to fact, typically answered by a clause beginning with la- ('then certainly…'). The leading wa- is the connector 'and'.

14.meaning: Men: adult male human beings. The plural noun denotes men as a group, sometimes carrying the sense of people of standing or strength.
14.grammar: A masculine plural noun (the plural of rajul, 'a man'). The -un ending is the nominative case with nunation, marking it as indefinite — 'men' rather than 'the men.'
14.root: ر-ج-ل (r-j-l) — man, manhood; also foot/on foot

15.meaning: Believers — those who believe; the masculine plural active participle of āmana. Here refers to the Muslim men among the inhabitants of Makkah who were not known to the attacking army.

parts.en: believers (masculine plural nominative, Form IV active participle)

15.grammar: Definite (contextually) active participle Form IV (āmana → muʾmin), masculine sound plural in the nominative case (marfūʿ), marked by /-ūna/.
15.root: أ-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — to be safe, to trust; Form IV: to believe; muʾmin = believer

16.meaning: And women — in addition to men among the hidden believers of Makkah, there were also believing women whom the attacking army might unknowingly harm.
16.grammar: Conjunction wāw + indefinite plural noun nisāʾ in the nominative case (marfūʿ), marked by tanwīn ḍamm (-un).
16.root: ن-س-و (n-s-w) — women; nisāʾ = women (irregular plural of imraʾa)

17.meaning: Believing women — the female believers of Makkah, whose presence prevented the attack. The feminine counterpart to muʾminūn.
17.grammar: Indefinite active participle Form IV, feminine sound plural in the nominative case, marked by tanwīn ḍamm + tāʾ marbūṭa pattern (/-ātun/).
17.root: أ-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — to believe; muʾmināt = believing women (feminine plural)

18.meaning: The particle 'lam', a negating word used to push a verb into the past: it means 'did not' / 'has not'. Though it sits before a present-tense verb form, it negates the action as something that did not happen.
18.grammar: 'lam' is a negating particle that governs a following present-tense verb but gives it past meaning ('did not …'). It also puts that verb into the shortened (jussive) form. 'lam' itself carries no ending.

19.meaning: You knew them / you recognised them — if you had known (the believing men and women), you could have avoided harming them. A conditional: had the believers been distinguishable, the Makkan believers would not have been at risk.

parts.en: you (pl.) know / recognised (2nd masc. pl. imperfect subjunctive/conditional)

19.grammar: Imperfect verb in subjunctive mood (or conditional use), 2nd person masculine plural, Form I (ʿalima — to know), with attached 3rd person masculine plural object pronoun.

20.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
20.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

21.meaning: You may trample / crush them — harm them unintentionally by marching over them or killing them accidentally (as they are mixed among the enemy population). A feared outcome that would bring moral harm upon the believers.

parts.en: you (pl.) may trample / crush (2nd masc. pl. subjunctive, Form I)

21.grammar: Imperfect verb in subjunctive mood, 2nd person masculine plural, Form I (waṭiʾa — to trample, to tread upon), with attached 3rd person masculine plural object pronoun.
21.root: و-ط-أ (w-ṭ-ʾ) — to tread, to trample; waṭʾ = treading, trampling

22.meaning: And it would befall you / and it would strike you — a misfortune or harm would come upon the believers: the moral harm of inadvertently harming innocents.

parts.en: it may befall (3rd fem. sg. subjunctive)

22.grammar: Consecutive fa + imperfect verb in subjunctive mood, 3rd person feminine singular, Form IV (aṣāba — to hit, to befall), with attached 2nd person masculine plural object pronoun.
22.root: ص-و-ب (ṣ-w-b) — to hit, to reach; Form IV: to befall, to afflict; iṣāba = affliction, misfortune

23.meaning: 'Among them / from them / some of them' — the preposition 'min' ('from, of, among') joined to the attached pronoun 'hum' ('them').
23.grammar: The preposition 'min' ('from / of / among') with the attached pronoun 'hum' ('them'), referring to a masculine plural group. Together they often express 'part of them' or 'some among them'.

24.meaning: Harm / injury / disgrace — the negative consequence (moral stain or social harm) that would befall the believers if they harmed hidden Muslim believers unknowingly. maʿarra denotes a blemish, harm, or cause for blame.

parts.en: harm / moral stain / disgrace (indefinite feminine nominative)

24.grammar: Indefinite feminine noun in the nominative case (marfūʿ), marked by tanwīn ḍamm. Pattern maFʿaLa (مَفْعَلَة).
24.root: ع-ر-ر (ʿ-r-r) — to harm, to wrong; maʿarra = harm, blemish, cause for blame

25.meaning: 'Without' or 'other than' — the preposition bi- joined to ghayr, a noun meaning 'other than / not / lacking', together conveying the absence of something ('with no …', 'wrongfully').
25.grammar: bi- is a preposition that takes the genitive; ghayr is a noun of exception/negation ('other than'). Its -i ending is genitive (required after bi-) and it also links to a following noun in a possessive 'of' relationship, so 'bi-ghayri X' means 'without X / other than X'.
25.root: غ-ي-ر (gh-y-r) — otherness, difference, being other than

26.meaning: 'Knowledge.' A noun denoting sure, established knowing — to know a thing as it truly is. In its indefinite form it often appears in the sense 'any knowledge (at all).'
26.grammar: A noun with the -in ending (genitive with nunation, 'tanwīn'), marking it as indefinite ('any knowledge'). The genitive -i is the form used after a preposition such as 'of' or 'by' — e.g. 'of any knowledge.'

27.meaning: So that He may admit — the divine purpose of withholding the believers from attacking Makkah: so that Allah could bring the hidden believers to safety and admit whomever He wills to His mercy.

parts.en: He may admit / cause to enter (3rd masc. sg. subjunctive, Form IV)

27.grammar: Lām al-taʿlīl + imperfect verb in subjunctive mood, 3rd person masculine singular, Form IV (adkhala).
27.root: د-خ-ل (d-kh-l) — to enter; Form IV: to admit, to cause to enter

28.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
28.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

29.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
29.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

30.meaning: His mercy — His compassion, tenderness, and loving-kindness that actively bestows good and relief. "Raḥmah" is mercy as an outpouring of care, here possessed by Him.
30.grammar: A feminine singular noun with an attached possessive "His." The -i ending is genitive: it typically links the word to a preceding noun or preposition ("… of …"). The pronoun appears as -hi (rather than -hu) because it follows that -i vowel.

31.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
31.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.

32.meaning: A present-tense verb meaning 'he wills, he wishes, he chooses' — to want or intend something by one's own decision.
32.grammar: A present/ongoing action by a single masculine subject ('he'); the ya- prefix marks third-person masculine singular, and the final -u marks the indicative mood — a plain statement of fact ('he wills'), as opposed to a command or a verb governed by 'that.'
32.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʾ) — willing, wishing; the root behind 'thing' (shayʾ)

33.meaning: A conditional particle introducing a hypothetical or contrary-to-fact supposition: 'if (it were the case that…)'. It typically presents a condition that is unfulfilled or merely imagined, often implying the result did not or would not happen.
33.grammar: An indeclinable particle (no case ending). It signals a hypothetical 'if': it sets up a supposed condition whose consequence is then stated, frequently with the sense 'if X were so, then Y would be so' — often where X is contrary to fact.

34.meaning: They had been separated / they were apart from each other — a past tense expressing the condition that would need to be true: if the believers and unbelievers of Makkah had been separated (clearly distinguishable), the attack might have proceeded.

parts.en: they were separated / apart (3rd masc. pl. past, Form V)

34.grammar: Past tense verb, 3rd person masculine plural, Form V (tazayyala — to be separated, to be apart).
34.root: ز-ي-ل (z-y-l) — to separate, to part; Form V: to be separated from each other

35.meaning: We would certainly have punished — a hypothetical statement: if the hidden believers had been separable, Allah would have punished the unbelievers severely. The lām is a lām al-tawkīd (emphasis) in a conditional response.

parts.en: We would have punished (1st pl. past, Form II)

35.grammar: Lām of emphasis (jawāb al-law) + past tense verb, 1st person plural, Form II (ʿadhdhaba — to punish).
35.root: ع-ذ-ب (ʿ-dh-b) — to punish; Form II: to punish severely; ʿadhāb = punishment

36.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
36.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

37.meaning: 'They disbelieved / rejected faith' — from a root meaning to cover over or conceal. To disbelieve in this sense is to cover up and refuse the truth, and also to be ungrateful, hiding or denying favours received.
37.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third person masculine plural: 'they disbelieved'. The completed action is built into the stem kafara ('he disbelieved'), and the -ū suffix (written وا) marks the doer as 'they' (masculine plural). The silent alif written after the -ū is a spelling convention with no sound.
37.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; to reject faith, be ungrateful

38.meaning: From them / among them — the preposition min ('from, out of, part of') joined to the pronoun 'them' (a group of males or a mixed group).
38.grammar: The preposition min ('from / among / part of') with the attached third-person masculine plural pronoun -hum ('them'). Pronouns after a preposition are in the genitive; the combination expresses origin, partition ('some of them'), or belonging to that group.

39.meaning: 'A punishment / torment.' A noun naming chastisement or painful suffering inflicted as a penalty.
39.grammar: A masculine noun. The -an ending marks it as indefinite ('a punishment') and in the accusative case — the form a noun takes as the object of a verb or as the thing being described/quantified.

40.meaning: An adjective meaning 'painful, agonizing, causing severe pain,' describing something that inflicts intense suffering.
40.grammar: An adjective in the intensive faʿīl pattern, which heightens the quality (deeply/intensely painful). The final -an (tanwīn fatḥa) marks it as indefinite ('a painful one') and in the accusative case — the case typically used for the object of a verb or for a describing word agreeing with such a noun.

1.meaning: A particle meaning 'when' or 'at the time that', used to point back to a past moment or event and introduce a recollection of something that occurred.
1.grammar: An indeclinable particle (it has no case ending and never changes form). It signals a point in past time, typically introducing a clause that recalls 'the time when' something happened.

2.meaning: 'He made,' 'He appointed,' 'He set up' — to bring about, fashion, or assign something to a state or role. Beyond mere 'making,' it often means rendering one thing into another or establishing something for a purpose.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb. The stem is the three root letters; the '-a' ending on it marks 'he' as the doer and places the action in the completed past ('he made / appointed'). This verb commonly governs two objects, in the sense of 'made X into Y.'
2.root: ج-ع-ل (j-ʿ-l) — to make, render, appoint

3.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
3.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

4.meaning: 'They disbelieved / rejected faith' — from a root meaning to cover over or conceal. To disbelieve in this sense is to cover up and refuse the truth, and also to be ungrateful, hiding or denying favours received.
4.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third person masculine plural: 'they disbelieved'. The completed action is built into the stem kafara ('he disbelieved'), and the -ū suffix (written وا) marks the doer as 'they' (masculine plural). The silent alif written after the -ū is a spelling convention with no sound.
4.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; to reject faith, be ungrateful

5.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
5.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

6.meaning: A noun meaning 'hearts' — the plural of the heart, understood as the inner seat of feeling, understanding, intention, and faith, not merely the physical organ.
6.grammar: A plural noun. The -i vowel on the stem is the genitive ending, which links the noun to what follows or follows a preposition ('… of …'); the attached -him(u) means 'their', so together it reads 'their hearts'. The final short -u is a connecting vowel that smooths pronunciation before the next word.
6.root: ق-ل-ب (q-l-b) — heart; turning over

7.meaning: The disdain / the arrogance / the zealotry — al-ḥamiyya: the spirit of tribal pride, blind zealotry, and stubborn arrogance that the unbelievers displayed at Hudaybiyyah. It is the narrow-minded pride of tribalism that rejects truth.

parts.en: the disdain / arrogance / zealotry (definite feminine accusative)

7.grammar: Definite feminine noun in the accusative case (manṣūb), marked by -a ending. ḥamiyya = zeal, fierce pride, protectiveness.
7.root: ح-م-ي (ḥ-m-y) — to protect, to be zealous; ḥamiyya = pride, tribal zeal, arrogance

8.meaning: The disdain of / zealotry of — the same noun as the previous entry but in the construct state (iḍāfa), meaning 'the zealotry/arrogance of ignorance (jāhiliyya).' Refers to pre-Islamic tribal pride.
8.grammar: Indefinite feminine noun in the accusative case in construct (iḍāfa) with jāhiliyya.
8.root: ح-م-ي (ḥ-m-y) — to protect; ḥamiyya = pride, arrogance, zealotry

9.meaning: Pre-Islamic ignorance — the state and outlook of heedless, godless ignorance, especially the customs, pride, and false beliefs of the age before guidance. An abstract noun for that condition of unenlightenment.
9.grammar: A definite abstract noun formed with the -iyya suffix (which turns a word into a named state or "-ism"), here ending in -i, which is genitive. This ending typically links the word to a preceding noun ("… OF …") or follows a preposition.
9.root: ج-ه-ل (j-h-l) — ignorance, not knowing; also reckless, hot-headed behavior

10.meaning: A verb meaning 'and/then he sent down / caused to descend,' the act of bringing something down from a higher place (often used of revelation, rain, or aid descending from Allah).
10.grammar: A perfect (past-tense) verb of the causative (Form IV) pattern 'anzala,' 3rd person masculine singular, prefixed with the connector fa- ('so/then'). The a- prefix turns 'to descend' into 'to send/bring down.' The final -a marks 'he' as the doer of a completed action: 'so He sent down.'

11.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
11.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

12.meaning: His tranquillity / His calm reassurance — a settling peace and steadiness that descends upon the heart, removing fear and agitation. Sakīna is an Allah-given serenity and composure.

parts.en: tranquillity / serene calm (with tā' marbūṭa surfacing as -t- before the pronoun)

12.grammar: A noun with the attached pronoun -hu ('his/its'). Its feminine ending (tā' marbūṭa) is pronounced -t- here because a suffix follows. The -a vowel before the pronoun is the accusative case, the form a noun takes when it is the direct object of a verb — the thing that is given, sent down, or acted upon.
12.root: س-ك-ن (s-k-n) — stillness, rest, calm, settling down

13.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
13.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

14.meaning: 'His Messenger' — a messenger or envoy, one sent with a message, here possessed by 'Him'.
14.grammar: A noun ('messenger') with the attached possessive pronoun -hi ('his'). The -i ending before the pronoun is genitive, typically signalling that the word follows a preposition or is the second term of a possessive phrase ('… of …'); the pronoun appears as -hi (rather than -hu) because of that preceding i vowel.
14.root: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — to send; a sending, message, messenger

15.meaning: A two-part phrase: the joining word 'and' plus the preposition 'on / upon / incumbent upon,' often used to express an obligation resting on someone.
15.grammar: The connector 'wa' ('and') joined to the preposition 'ʿalā' ('upon'). Both are indeclinable particles with no case ending; a noun governed by 'ʿalā' takes the genitive.

16.meaning: A plural noun meaning 'the believers' — those who have faith, who inwardly trust and affirm. The Form IV participle denotes one who brings about belief and security within.
16.grammar: A definite plural active participle of Form IV (āmana 'to believe'). The -īna ending marks a sound masculine plural in the accusative/genitive (object or oblique) state. The prefixed mu- marks it as a Form IV participle ('one who has/gives faith').

17.meaning: And He made them adhere / He obligated them to stick to — Allah bound them firmly to something (the word of taqwā / restraint). A divine act of fixing or attaching something to someone's heart.

parts.en: He obligated / made adhere (3rd masc. sg. past, Form IV)

17.grammar: Conjunction wāw + past tense verb, 3rd person masculine singular, Form IV (alzama — to oblige, to make compulsory, to bind), with attached 3rd person masculine plural object pronoun.
17.root: ل-ز-م (l-z-m) — to be necessary, to adhere; Form IV: to make binding, to oblige; ilzām = obligation

18.meaning: A noun meaning 'word, utterance, statement,' or by extension a 'cause,' 'message,' or 'decree' expressed in words.
18.grammar: A feminine singular noun. The final -a is the accusative case ending, which typically marks the word as a direct object of a verb, or as otherwise grammatically governed into the accusative. The 't' of the feminine ending (tā' marbūṭa) is pronounced here because a case vowel follows it.

19.meaning: Taqwā — God-consciousness: a reverent awareness of Allah that moves one to guard against wrongdoing and to do what is right. It is a protective mindfulness, 'guarding oneself' by keeping Allah ever in view.
19.grammar: A noun with the definite article 'al-' ('the'). It ends in a fixed long vowel ('-ā', written as alif maqṣūra) which does not change for case; such words show their grammatical role only by context, not by a changing ending.

20.meaning: A compound meaning 'and they were' or 'and they used to' — it sets a state or habit in the past. The verb 'to be/become' here establishes an ongoing past condition, often paired with a following verb to express habitual action.
20.grammar: A past-tense verb ('to be') in the third-person masculine plural — the -ū ending means 'they' did/were. It commonly conveys a continued past state or habit, especially when followed by another verb. The wa- prefix means 'and.'
20.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to come into being

21.meaning: More deserving / more worthy / more entitled — the elative (comparative/superlative) form: ahaqq means 'most deserving of' or 'more entitled to.' Here it indicates that the believers were more worthy of the terms of Hudaybiyyah.
21.grammar: Elative adjective (afʿal pattern), masculine singular in the accusative case, taking a genitive complement. Diptote.
21.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — to be true, to be right; ḥaqq = right, truth; aḥaqq = more deserving/worthy

22.meaning: with it / by it — a preposition meaning 'with' or 'by means of' joined to a pronoun referring to a single feminine (or grammatically feminine) thing.
22.grammar: The bi- prefix is a preposition meaning 'with', 'by', or 'by means of'. The attached -hā is an object pronoun meaning 'it' or 'her', referring to something feminine in gender. Together they mean 'with it' or 'by means of it'.

23.meaning: And its people / and those entitled to it — those who deserve it or belong to it. Refers to the believers being the true people of Makkah and the true heirs of the Kaʿba.

parts.en: it / its (3rd fem. sg. possessive pronoun)

23.grammar: Conjunction wāw + masculine noun ahl in the accusative case in construct (iḍāfa) with the attached 3rd person feminine singular possessive pronoun.
23.root: أ-ه-ل (ʾ-h-l) — family, people; ahl = people of / worthy

24.meaning: And he was / he became — a verb of being that places a subject in a past state or links it to a description in the past.
24.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'kāna' is a past-tense verb, 3rd-person masculine singular, meaning 'he was/became'; it commonly introduces a past condition and is typically followed by a noun describing the subject's state. The final -a marks completed past action by a single male.

25.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
25.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

26.meaning: 'Of every / with all' — the preposition 'bi' ('with / in / by') joined to the word 'every / each / all', expressing comprehensiveness applied to whatever noun follows.
26.grammar: A preposition plus a noun. The prefix bi- ('with / in / by') always places the following noun in the genitive ('of') state. The final -i on 'kull' is that genitive ending, signalling the word is governed by the preposition. 'Kull' denotes totality — 'every (single)' or 'all'.

27.meaning: 'a thing' — anything that exists or can be conceived, an entity or matter in the most general sense. It is the broadest Arabic word for 'something,' covering objects, affairs, and abstractions alike.
27.grammar: An indefinite singular noun. The '-in' ending (tanwīn al-kasr) signals two things at once: indefiniteness ('a thing,' not 'the thing') and the genitive case, marking it as following a preposition or completing a possessive link to a preceding noun.
27.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʼ) — to will, to be a thing/existent

28.meaning: 'All-Knowing', 'fully aware' — possessing complete and thorough knowledge; one who knows perfectly.
28.grammar: An intensive adjective on the 'faʿīl' pattern, conveying deep, complete knowledge. The '-an' ending is the indefinite accusative with nunation; this case is used for direct objects and for the second part of certain verbs of being ('was … all-knowing').

1.meaning: A two-part emphasis particle meaning 'surely, indeed (already)' — 'la-' strongly affirms, and 'qad' before a past verb stresses that the action has definitely occurred.
1.grammar: Two particles fused for emphasis. 'la-' is the affirming prefix 'surely / truly.' 'qad,' when it precedes a past-tense verb, confirms and intensifies that the action really happened ('has indeed …'). Together they give a strong oath-like assurance to the statement that follows.

2.meaning: 'He spoke the truth; he was truthful; what he said proved true' — affirming that a person told the truth or that a statement is true and reliable.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb, 3rd person masculine singular ('he spoke the truth'). This is the basic (Form I) verb pattern. The final '-a' is the standard past-tense ending for 'he,' marking a completed act by a single male subject.
2.root: ص-د-ق (ṣ-d-q) — to be truthful, speak truly, be sincere

3.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
3.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.
3.root: — (proper divine name)

4.meaning: His Messenger — the Messenger belonging to Allah (rasūl + possessive pronoun -hu). The Prophet Muhammad, Allah's chosen envoy sent with the final revelation.
4.grammar: Masculine noun rasūl in the accusative case in construct (iḍāfa) with the 3rd person masculine singular possessive pronoun -hu.
4.root: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — to send; rasūl = messenger, one sent

5.meaning: The vision — a noun for something seen, especially a dream-vision or a sight beheld (as opposed to ordinary seeing).
5.grammar: A definite feminine verbal noun formed with al- ('the'). It ends in a fixed long -ā (a feminine ending), so its case does not change form — it reads the same whether subject, object, or possessed.

6.meaning: 'With the truth / by means of what is true and right.' Combines the preposition 'with/by' and 'the truth' — that which is real, established, correct, and rightfully due, as opposed to falsehood.
6.grammar: A noun governed by the attached preposition bi- ('with/by'). The -i ending is the genitive case, which is required after a preposition; here it links 'the truth' to 'with', giving 'with the truth'.
6.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — truth, right, reality, that which is established and due

7.meaning: You will surely enter — a strong emphatic future affirmation: 'You will certainly enter (the Sacred Mosque).' The lām + nūn al-tawkīd (nūn of emphasis) together make the assertion definite and emphatic.

parts.en: you (pl.) will enter (2nd masc. pl. imperfect + nūn tawkīd)

7.grammar: Lām of tawkīd + imperfect verb, 2nd person masculine plural, Form I (dakhala — to enter), with heavy nūn al-tawkīd attached (changing -ūna to -unna).
7.root: د-خ-ل (d-kh-l) — to enter; dukhūl = entering, admission

8.meaning: A place of prostration; a mosque — the building or site where the act of bowing down in worship (sujūd) is performed.
8.grammar: A noun of place built on the pattern maf'il, naming the location where an action happens — here 'the place of prostration.' The definite article al- marks it as 'the.' The -a ending is accusative (object case): it typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb (the thing being acted upon).
8.root: س-ج-د (s-j-d) — to prostrate, bow down

9.meaning: 'the forbidden / the sacred / the inviolable' — that which is set apart as holy and protected, so that violating it is prohibited. It applies to sacred places, months, and things whose sanctity must not be breached.
9.grammar: An adjective/noun carrying 'the'. The final -a ending is accusative; because the word already has 'the', it takes a plain -a (no 'n' sound). The accusative typically marks a direct object or describes such an object.
9.root: ح-ر-م (ḥ-r-m) — to be forbidden, sacred, inviolable

10.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
10.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

11.meaning: A past-tense verb 'he willed / he wished / he so desired'. It denotes an act of will or volition bringing something about.
11.grammar: Past-tense (perfect) verb, third person masculine singular ('he'). The bare stem with no suffix is the basic 'he did' form. Its subject and object are typically supplied by context.

12.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
12.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

13.meaning: 'Safe, secure, free from fear' — those who are in a state of security and peace, with nothing to dread.
13.grammar: An active participle (a doer/state noun) meaning 'one who is secure', in the sound masculine plural. The -īna ending marks the accusative/genitive ('oblique') case — used when the word is an object, follows a preposition, or describes such a noun, in contrast to the -ūna subject form.

14.meaning: Having shaved (their heads) — a circumstantial participle: the believers will enter the Sacred Mosque with their heads shaved, which is one of the rituals that marks the completion of Hajj or ʿUmra.

parts.en: having shaved (their heads) (masculine plural oblique, active participle Form II)

14.grammar: Definite active participle Form II (ḥallaqa — to shave, to make smooth), masculine sound plural in the oblique (accusative/genitive) case, marked by /-īna/.
14.root: ح-ل-ق (ḥ-l-q) — to shave (the head); Form II: to shave completely; taḥlīq = head-shaving (Hajj ritual)

15.meaning: Your heads — the uppermost part of the body, here the plural belonging to a group of people.
15.grammar: A plural noun with an attached possessive pronoun. The -a is the accusative ending, marking the noun as the direct object of a verb. The suffix -kum means 'your' for a group ('you all').

16.meaning: And having cut / trimmed — those who trim their hair instead of shaving it completely. Both shaving and trimming are valid conclusions to Hajj/ʿUmra.

parts.en: those who trim / shorten (masculine plural oblique, active participle Form II)

16.grammar: Conjunction wāw + definite active participle Form II (qaṣṣara — to trim, to shorten), masculine sound plural in the oblique case (/-īna/).
16.root: ق-ص-ر (q-ṣ-r) — to be short, to fall short; Form II: to trim/shorten (hair); taqṣīr = trimming

17.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
17.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

18.meaning: You fear, dread, or apprehend — to be afraid of something or to anticipate a feared outcome.
18.grammar: A present/imperfect verb, second person masculine plural ('you all'). The ta- prefix marks 'you', and the -ūna ending marks a plural subject in the indicative mood, typically describing an ongoing or general action ('you (all) fear').

19.meaning: And He knew — past tense: Allah perceived and knew something (specifically, what was in the hearts of the believers at Hudaybiyyah). Divine knowledge preceding and encompassing all events.
19.grammar: Consecutive fa + past tense verb, 3rd person masculine singular, Form I (ʿalima — to know).

20.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
20.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

21.meaning: A negating particle, 'not', used specifically to deny that an action happened in the past, even though it attaches to a present-tense verb form. It turns 'you do X' into 'you did not do X'.

parts.en: did not (negation of a completed act)

21.grammar: An indeclinable particle that governs the verb after it, putting that verb into the jussive (clipped) mood and giving it past-time meaning. In short: lam + a present-form verb = 'did not [verb]'.

22.meaning: You (plural) know, understand, or have knowledge of something — grasping a fact with certainty.
22.grammar: A present-tense verb. The ta- prefix marks a second-person subject ('you'), and the -ū ending makes it masculine plural ('you all'). The short, vowelless -ū (not -ūna) is the jussive/subjunctive shape, used after particles of command, negation, or purpose ('until you know' / 'so that you know').

23.meaning: And He made / and He appointed — Allah ordained or arranged something. Here used of Allah establishing the conquest of Makkah or the vision of the Prophet as a truth.

parts.en: He made / appointed (3rd masc. sg. past, Form I)

23.grammar: Consecutive fa + past tense verb, 3rd person masculine singular, Form I (jaʿala — to make, to appoint, to set).
23.root: ج-ع-ل (j-ʿ-l) — to make, to place, to appoint; jaʿl = making, placing

24.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
24.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

25.meaning: A noun used to mean 'besides', 'other than', 'apart from', or 'short of'. It points to something or someone set apart from, or lower/lesser than, a named party. Often used in the phrase 'besides Allah'.
25.grammar: 'dūn' functions as an adverb-like noun of place/relation. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, which appears because it follows a preposition (such as 'min', 'from') and because it links to a following noun ('other than …'). It commonly heads the construction 'besides/other than [someone]'.
25.root: د-و-ن (d-w-n) — to be low/beneath, to fall short; hence 'below, other than, besides'

26.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that' — pointing to something regarded as distant or elevated, as opposed to 'this' (hadha) for what is near. It singles out a masculine singular thing and lends it a sense of distinction or loftiness.
26.grammar: A demonstrative for a masculine singular referent at a distance. The -ka ending is an address particle directed at a single male listener; it does not change for case. The whole word stays fixed in form regardless of its grammatical position.

27.meaning: A clear, manifest opening or victory — a decisive triumph that removes an obstacle and opens the way forward. In Qur'anic usage it denotes a victory granted by Allah that unfolds with clarity and completeness.
27.grammar: Indefinite masculine noun in the accusative case (manṣūb), marked by tanwīn fatḥ (-an). Serves as the object of the implied verb or predicate complement.
27.root: ف-ت-ح (f-t-ḥ) — to open, to conquer, to grant victory

28.meaning: An adjective meaning 'near, close, close at hand' — describing something short in distance, time, or relationship, easily reached or soon to come.
28.grammar: A masculine singular adjective on the 'faʿīl' pattern ('near, close'). The ending -an is the accusative case with tanwīn (nunation), which typically marks the word as agreeing with an accusative noun it describes, or otherwise governed into the accusative; the tanwīn shows it is indefinite.

1.meaning: 'He' — the standalone (independent) pronoun for a single masculine person or thing, used for emphasis or to stand as the subject on its own.
1.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, third-person masculine singular. It does not take case endings; its fixed final -a is part of the word. It serves to name or emphasize the subject ('He is the one who…').

2.meaning: A relative pronoun meaning 'the one who' or 'which' — it points back to a masculine singular person or thing and introduces a clause that describes or identifies it. It works like the English 'who/which/that' that opens a defining clause.
