2.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) masculine singular relative pronoun: its form does not change for case, so the ending stays -ī whatever grammatical role it fills. It always needs a following clause to complete its meaning.

3.meaning: To send, dispatch, or send forth — to commission someone or something and set it on its way toward a destination or purpose.
3.grammar: A past-tense verb (causative Form IV) for a third-person masculine singular subject: 'he sent' or 'he dispatched.' The a- prefix and the pattern give the causative sense (to cause to go / send off); the final -a is the standard 'he (did it)' past-tense ending.
3.root: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — sending, dispatching, commissioning a messenger

4.meaning: His messenger — an envoy, emissary, or apostle belonging to a single male sender; one sent to deliver a message on his behalf.
4.grammar: A masculine singular noun, 'messenger,' with the attached pronoun -hu ('his') marking a single male owner/sender. The -a vowel (accusative) typically marks the noun as the direct object of a verb ('… his messenger').
4.root: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — sending; a messenger is 'one who is sent'

5.meaning: A two-part expression meaning 'with/through the guidance'. It combines the preposition 'with/by means of' and the noun hudā — right guidance, the clear showing of the correct way and being led upon it.
5.grammar: The preposition bi- ('with/by') attached to the definite noun al-hudā ('the guidance'). Because hudā ends in a fixed long vowel (a 'frozen' ending), its case does not visibly change after the preposition, though it stands in the genitive that bi- requires.
5.root: ه-د-ي (h-d-y) — to guide, lead rightly, show the way

6.meaning: And religion — a way of life, system of belief, worship, and obedience owed to a higher authority; also recompense or the binding code one lives by. Dīn carries the sense of a complete path one is accountable to, not merely private belief.
6.grammar: The wa- prefix means 'and,' joining this to what precedes. The noun 'religion' carries the -i (genitive) ending, which typically links it to a following noun ('the religion OF …') or follows a preposition or possessive construction.
6.root: د-ي-ن (d-y-n) — religion, way of life; obedience, recompense

7.meaning: 'The truth', 'the right', 'what is rightfully due' — that which is real, correct, and justly owed; the opposite of falsehood and wrongdoing.
7.grammar: A definite masculine noun (the al- prefix means 'the'). The -i ending is genitive, the case typically taken after a preposition or when the word links to a preceding noun ('… of the truth / by right').
7.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — truth, rightness, that which is established and due

8.meaning: So that he may make it prevail, manifest it, or cause it to triumph and become dominant over all else.
8.grammar: The li- prefix means 'so that' or 'in order to,' expressing purpose. The verb is present-tense (causative Form IV) for a 'he' subject — to cause to appear, make manifest, or make victorious — and the purpose particle forces the special -a ending (subjunctive) heard as 'yuẓhira.' The attached -hu ('it/him') is the object being made to prevail.
8.root: ظ-ه-ر (ẓ-h-r) — appearing, becoming manifest; prevailing, gaining the upper hand

9.meaning: 'To / before / upon' — a preposition whose core sense is being on top of, above, or directed onto something; with a verb of presenting it carries the directional sense 'to / before / in front of,' and it can also convey obligation ('incumbent upon').
9.grammar: A preposition. Its basic meaning is 'on, upon, over,' but with verbs of displaying or presenting it shades into 'to / before / in front of.' It governs the following noun in the genitive case. It is fixed in form and takes no changing ending of its own (its final long -ā is an unchanging part of the word).
9.root: — (preposition; loosely related to the sense of 'height/elevation')

10.meaning: A term for 'the religion, the faith, the way of life and obedience owed to Allah'. It covers belief, worship, law, and the system of accountability and recompense — broader than the English word 'religion'.
10.grammar: A definite noun ('the religion'); the al- prefix means 'the'. The -i ending is genitive, the case used after a preposition or in a possessive link ('… of …').
10.root: د-ي-ن (d-y-n) — religion, judgment, requital, obedience, debt

11.meaning: 'All of it / the whole of it' — a word denoting entirety or totality, here joined to a pronoun meaning 'it', giving 'the whole of it, every part of it'.
11.grammar: A noun meaning 'all/the totality', used in apposition for emphasis. It is in the genitive (the -i before the pronoun), the case used after a preposition or in a possessive link. The attached -hi is the pronoun 'it/his' ('all of it').
11.root: ك-ل-ل (k-l-l) — wholeness, totality, the sum of parts

12.meaning: 'And He suffices / is enough' — to be sufficient, adequate, and fully enough so that nothing more is needed. It conveys complete adequacy, often used to affirm that Allah alone is enough.
12.grammar: The connective wa- ('and') prefixed to a 3rd-person masculine singular perfect (past-tense) verb (Form I) whose final weak root letter (the yāʾ) appears as a long -ā. It states a completed yet timeless fact — 'and He is sufficient' — the kind of perfect form used for an enduring truth.
12.root: ك-ف-ي (k-f-y) — to suffice, be enough, be adequate; to spare someone need of anything else

13.meaning: A phrase 'in Allah / by Allah', combining the preposition 'with/in/by' and the divine name Allah, the proper name of the One God.
13.grammar: The preposition bi- ('in, with, by means of') prefixed to the divine name Allah. A preposition always forces the following noun into the genitive case, which is why Allah here ends in -i. With verbs of believing, bi- conveys the object of faith — to believe IN.
13.root: — (Allah is the proper name of God and is not derived from a triliteral root in the usual sense)

14.meaning: 'A witness' — one who sees and attests, who can give evidence; also carries the sense of one who is present and observant, and at times 'a martyr' (one who bears witness with their life).
14.grammar: An intensive describing-noun (pattern fa‘īl) meaning 'a witness, one who fully attests', indefinite. The -an ending (the accusative with 'tanwīn') marks it as indefinite and in the accusative — the case used for a direct object, or for a word that describes the state or role in which someone stands.

1.meaning: Muḥammad — a masculine proper name meaning 'the praised one' or 'one worthy of much praise', built on the pattern of intensive/repeated praise.
1.grammar: A proper name of the passive-participle 'mufaʿʿal' (intensive) pattern, meaning 'highly praised'. The final -un (nunation) marks it as nominative — the case used for a subject or for the thing being identified/named.

2.meaning: (Is the) Messenger — rasūl here refers to the Prophet Muhammad as the Messenger of Allah, used in the context of describing his role and that of his Companions.
2.grammar: Masculine noun rasūl in the nominative case (marfūʿ), marked by -u (ḍamma). Subject or part of a nominal sentence.
2.root: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — to send; rasūl = messenger, envoy

3.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
3.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

4.meaning: 'And those who': a connective phrase introducing a specified group of people (masculine plural) about whom something will be said. It links them to what came before.
4.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to the relative pronoun alladhīna ('those who'), which is masculine plural. A relative pronoun stands for a group and is normally followed by a clause describing them. Its form does not change for case; it stays alladhīna whatever its grammatical role.
4.root: — (relative pronoun)

5.meaning: Together with him; in his company or alongside him.
5.grammar: An adverb of accompaniment, 'with', joined to the attached pronoun -hu 'him'. Together they mean 'with him / in his company'.

6.meaning: Firm / severe / strict — those who are strong and unyielding against the enemies of Allah. Plural of shadīd, here used as a predicate: the Companions are firm/severe toward the unbelievers.
6.grammar: Broken plural of shadīd (شَدِيد — strong, severe), in the nominative case (marfūʿ) as predicate.
6.root: ش-د-د (sh-d-d) — to tighten, to be strong/severe; shadīd = severe; ashiddāʾ = pl. firm, severe

7.meaning: 'To / before / upon' — a preposition whose core sense is being on top of, above, or directed onto something; with a verb of presenting it carries the directional sense 'to / before / in front of,' and it can also convey obligation ('incumbent upon').
7.grammar: A preposition. Its basic meaning is 'on, upon, over,' but with verbs of displaying or presenting it shades into 'to / before / in front of.' It governs the following noun in the genitive case. It is fixed in form and takes no changing ending of its own (its final long -ā is an unchanging part of the word).
7.root: — (preposition; loosely related to the sense of 'height/elevation')

8.meaning: The disbelievers / the ungrateful — those who reject faith and cover over the truth. The plural form (kuffār) stresses persistent, often defiant denial; the root sense is 'to cover/conceal,' hence to deny what is true and be ungrateful.
8.grammar: A definite plural noun (intensive pattern fuʿʿāl) with the article al- ('the'). The final -i is genitive: it typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… of the disbelievers') or follows a preposition.
8.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; to disbelieve, be ungrateful

9.meaning: Merciful / compassionate — plural of raḥīm; the Companions are merciful toward each other (fellow believers), showing tenderness and care within the Muslim community.
9.grammar: Broken plural of raḥīm (رَحِيم — merciful), in the nominative case (marfūʿ) as predicate.
9.root: ر-ح-م (r-ḥ-m) — mercy, compassion; raḥīm = merciful; ruḥamāʾ = pl. merciful ones

10.meaning: An adverb of place meaning 'between' or 'among', here joined to the attached pronoun 'them'; together it conveys 'between them / amongst them', signalling something situated in the midst of a group or shared among parties.
10.grammar: An adverb of place (ẓarf) ending in -a, the accusative marker typical of such adverbs, indicating a location or relationship. The attached suffix '-hum' is a possessive/object pronoun meaning 'them' (a group of males or a mixed group).
10.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — separation, distinction, what lies in the midst

11.meaning: You see them — an address to the observer/reader: 'You will observe them (the Companions)...' — directing attention to a visible scene of the believers in prayer.

parts.en: you see them (2nd masc. sg. imperfect + 3rd pl. object pronoun)

11.grammar: Imperfect verb, indicative mood, 2nd person masculine singular, Form I (raʾā → tarā, hollow verb), with attached 3rd person masculine plural object pronoun -hum.
11.root: ر-أ-ي (r-ʾ-y) — to see; tarā = you see (present/imperfect of raʾā)

12.meaning: Bowing / in a state of rukūʿ — performing the rukūʿ (bowing position in prayer). A circumstantial plural participle describing the posture of the believers at prayer.

parts.en: bowing / in rukūʿ (indefinite masculine plural accusative)

12.grammar: Indefinite broken plural of rākiʿ (رَاكِع — one who bows), in the accusative case as ḥāl (circumstantial complement).
12.root: ر-ك-ع (r-k-ʿ) — to bow, to bend; rukūʿ = the bowing in prayer; rākiʿ = one bowing; rukkaʿ = those bowing

13.meaning: 'Prostrating' / 'in prostration' — bowing down low with the face to the ground, the posture of deepest humility and worship. A plural describing a group in that humble, bowed state.
13.grammar: A plural active descriptor ('those prostrating'). The -an ending is the indefinite accusative, which here works adverbially — describing the manner or state in which the subject acts (i.e. doing something 'while prostrating'). The doubled middle letter marks the intensive plural pattern used for a group performing the action.
13.root: س-ج-د (s-j-d) — prostration, bowing down in worship

14.meaning: They seek / they desire — actively pursuing something. In the context of 48:29, the believers seek Allah's grace and pleasure through their devotion and prayer.

parts.en: they seek / desire (3rd masc. pl. imperfect indicative, Form VIII)

14.grammar: Imperfect verb, indicative mood, 3rd person masculine plural, Form VIII (ibtaghā — to seek, to desire). Marked by /-ūna/.
14.root: ب-غ-ي (b-gh-y) — to seek, to desire; Form VIII: ibtighaʾ = seeking

15.meaning: Bounty, grace, favour, or abundance; something good given freely and beyond what is owed. It can mean material provision (such as profit from trade) or divine grace and excess generosity.
15.grammar: A singular masculine noun. The final -an (accusative case with nunation) typically marks it as the direct object of a verb ('seeking a bounty') or as the goal of an action. The nunation also makes it indefinite ('a bounty / some favour').
15.root: ف-ض-ل (f-ḍ-l) — to be in excess, to surpass; hence grace, bounty, superiority

16.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
16.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

17.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
17.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

18.meaning: And pleasure / and contentment — the riḍwān of Allah: His divine approval and pleasure. One of the highest objectives for the believer — to earn Allah's contentment.
18.grammar: Conjunction wāw + indefinite masculine noun in the accusative case (manṣūb), marked by tanwīn fatḥ (-an).
18.root: ر-ض-و (r-ḍ-w) — to be pleased, to approve; riḍā/riḍwān = pleasure, contentment, approval

19.meaning: Their mark / their sign — the distinguishing feature or sign of the believers. In the context of 48:29, it refers to the mark of prostration (sijda) visible on their foreheads from frequent prayer.
19.grammar: Feminine noun sīmā (mark, sign, brand) in the nominative case in construct with the 3rd person masculine plural possessive pronoun.
19.root: س-و-م (s-w-m) — to mark, to brand; sīmā = mark, sign, distinguishing feature

20.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
20.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

21.meaning: Their faces — the face as the front of the head, here belonging to a group ('their'). The face often stands for a person's whole self or presence.
21.grammar: A broken plural noun ('faces') with an attached possessive pronoun -him ('their', masculine plural). The -i ending is genitive: it typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… of …') or follows a preposition. The pronoun takes the -i (rather than -u) vowel after this genitive ending.
21.root: و-ج-ه (w-j-h) — face, front, direction, that which one turns toward

22.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
22.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

23.meaning: 'Track' / 'trace, footprint, mark left behind' — the impression or remnant that something leaves after passing; that which follows in the wake of a thing.
23.grammar: A noun ('track, trace') ending in -i. This final -i is the noun's own genitive case ending (an inflectional vowel, not a separate suffix): it links the noun to a following noun in an 'of' relationship, or marks it as governed by a preceding preposition or particle.
23.root: ا-ث-ر (ʾ-th-r) — a trace, track, or mark left behind

24.meaning: Those who prostrate, or the act of prostration itself; relating to sujūd, placing the forehead on the ground in submission to Allah. The form can name a group of prostrating worshippers or the state of prostration.
24.grammar: A definite noun of the pattern fuʿūl, used as a verbal noun ('prostration') and also as a plural for those prostrating. The final -i ending is genitive: it typically links the word to a following noun ('… of …') or follows a preposition or oath particle.
24.root: س-ج-د (s-j-d) — to prostrate, bow the forehead to the ground

25.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that' — pointing to something regarded as distant or elevated, as opposed to 'this' (hadha) for what is near. It singles out a masculine singular thing and lends it a sense of distinction or loftiness.
25.grammar: A demonstrative for a masculine singular referent at a distance. The -ka ending is an address particle directed at a single male listener; it does not change for case. The whole word stays fixed in form regardless of its grammatical position.

26.meaning: Their likeness, parable, or comparable case — an illustrative example or similitude that depicts what something is like. The attached pronoun marks the example as pertaining to them.
26.grammar: A noun with the attached possessive -hum ('their,' for a group of males). The -u ending before the pronoun is nominative, the case typically marking the subject of a sentence or the thing being described.

27.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
27.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

28.meaning: The Torah — the revealed scripture given to the Prophet Moses (Mūsā).
28.grammar: The al- prefix means 'the' (its 'l' is pronounced as a doubled 't' merging into the following letter). The final -i is the genitive case, fitting a word that follows a preposition or is linked to a preceding noun ('… of the Torah'). Because it carries 'the', it takes a single -i (not tanwīn).

29.meaning: And their similitude / their likeness — a comparison being drawn: 'their likeness (in) the Gospel is...' Referring to the description of the Companions in the previous scriptures.
29.grammar: Conjunction wāw + masculine noun mathal in the nominative case (marfūʿ) in construct (iḍāfa) with the 3rd person masculine plural possessive suffix -hum.
29.root: م-ث-ل (m-th-l) — to resemble, to be like; mathal = parable, likeness, similitude

30.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
30.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

31.meaning: The Injeel / the Gospel — the holy scripture revealed to Prophet ʿĪsā (Jesus), before its later alteration. The Qur'an references a description of the Companions that was present in the original Gospel.
31.grammar: Definite noun (with the definite article) in the genitive case (majrūr) as the second element of the iḍāfa. Likely a loanword (Greek: euangelion).
31.root: — (loanword from Greek euangelion; ʾinjīl in Arabic)

32.meaning: Like a seed / like (a) planted grain — introducing the extended parable of the early Muslim community's growth, comparing them to a seed that sprouts, strengthens, and stands firm.
32.grammar: Comparative particle ka + indefinite masculine noun zarʿ in the genitive case (majrūr).
32.root: ز-ر-ع (z-r-ʿ) — to sow, to cultivate; zarʿ = crop, sown seed, agriculture

33.meaning: 'He brought out / expelled / drove out' — to make someone or something come out, the completed act of one male doer.
33.grammar: Past-tense verb in the causative pattern 'afʿala' ('akhraja' = to cause to go out). The bare stem with a final '-a' and no added subject marks a third-person masculine singular doer ('he') and a completed action.

34.meaning: Its shoot / its sprout — the young offshoot or new growth emerging from the seed. In the parable, this represents the early followers that began to emerge around the initial seed (the Prophet's message).
34.grammar: Masculine noun shaṭʾ (شَطْء — sprout, tiller, offshoot) in the accusative case in construct with the 3rd person masculine singular possessive suffix (referring to the seed, zarʿ).
34.root: ش-ط-أ (sh-ṭ-ʾ) — to sprout, to shoot forth; shaṭʾ = sprout, tiller, offshoot of a plant

35.meaning: Then it supports / strengthens it — the shoot reinforces the original stalk. The prefixed fa indicates sequence: the seed brings forth a shoot, and then that shoot supports and strengthens the main stalk.

parts.en: it strengthens / supports (3rd masc. sg. past, Form III)

35.grammar: Consecutive fa + past tense verb, 3rd person masculine singular, Form III (āzara — to strengthen, to support mutually), with attached 3rd person masculine singular object pronoun.
35.root: أ-ز-ر (ʾ-z-r) — to strengthen, to support; izār = loincloth (that supports/girds); Form III: to strengthen each other

36.meaning: Then it becomes thick / hardens — the plant grows stout and firm. Continuing the parable: after the shoot strengthens the stalk, the stalk becomes thick and robust.

parts.en: it became thick / hardened (3rd masc. sg. past, Form X)

36.grammar: Consecutive fa + past tense verb, 3rd person masculine singular, Form X (istaghallaẓa — to become or find something thick/coarse).
36.root: غ-ل-ظ (gh-l-ẓ) — to be thick, coarse, hard; ghilẓa = thickness; Form X: to become thick

37.meaning: Then it stands upright / levels itself — the plant grows to its full height and stands erect. In the parable, this represents the Muslim community reaching its strength and full stature.

parts.en: it stood upright / became even (3rd masc. sg. past, Form X)

37.grammar: Consecutive fa + past tense verb, 3rd person masculine singular, Form X (istawā — to be straight, to stand upright, to be level).
37.root: س-و-ي (s-w-y) — to be equal, to be level; Form X: istawā = to stand upright, to be even, to be balanced

38.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
38.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

39.meaning: Its stalk — the main stem or trunk of the plant on which it stands erect. The parable continues: the plant stands upon its stalk.

parts.en: its (3rd masc. sg. possessive, genitive form)

39.grammar: Masculine noun sūq (سُوق — stalk, stem of a plant) in the genitive case in construct with the 3rd person masculine singular possessive suffix.
39.root: س-و-ق (s-w-q) — to drive, stalk (of a plant); sūq here = stalk/stem of a plant

40.meaning: It delights / it amazes — the fully grown plant fills the farmers with wonder and admiration. Referring to the amazing, pleasing sight of a strong, full-grown crop.

parts.en: it delights / amazes (3rd masc. sg. imperfect indicative, Form IV)

40.grammar: Imperfect verb, indicative mood, 3rd person masculine singular, Form IV (aʿjaba — to amaze, to please, to delight).
40.root: ع-ج-ب (ʿ-j-b) — to be amazed; Form IV: to amaze, to delight; ʿajab = wonder, amazement

41.meaning: The sowers / the farmers — those who planted the seed. In the parable, they represent those who witness the growth of the Muslim community with admiration and awe.

parts.en: the sowers / farmers (definite masculine plural accusative)

41.grammar: Definite broken plural of zāriʿ (زَارِع — farmer, sower), in the accusative case (manṣūb) as the object of yuʿjibu.
41.root: ز-ر-ع (z-r-ʿ) — to sow, to plant; zāriʿ = sower; zurāʿ = farmers/sowers (plural)

42.meaning: So that He may enrage / infuriate — the divine purpose in making the believers a strong, thriving community: to provoke the anger of the unbelievers who see them flourish while being unable to stop them.

parts.en: He may enrage (3rd masc. sg. subjunctive, Form I)

42.grammar: Lām of purpose + imperfect verb in subjunctive mood, 3rd person masculine singular, Form I (ghāẓa → yaghīẓu → yaghīẓa in subjunctive).
42.root: غ-ي-ظ (gh-y-ẓ) — to enrage, to infuriate; ghaīẓ = rage, fury

43.meaning: 'By/with them' or 'for them' — the preposition bi ('with, by, through, for') joined to the attached pronoun 'them' (a masculine group).
43.grammar: The preposition bi- ('with, by, for') attached to the pronoun -him ('them', masculine plural). The final -u is a connecting vowel added so the word joins smoothly to whatever follows. The preposition naturally puts its pronoun in the genitive.

44.meaning: The disbelievers, those who reject faith — people who actively cover over and deny the truth and are ungrateful for it; an intensive plural stressing entrenched rejection.
44.grammar: An intensive plural on the pattern fuʿʿāl, stressing the strength of rejection. The prefix al- is the definite article 'the'. The final -a is the accusative case ending: it typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon). With the definite article there is no nunation.
44.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal, reject, be ungrateful

45.meaning: 'He promised / pledged' — a completed act of giving one's word that something will come about, whether a reward or a consequence.
45.grammar: A past-tense verb with no attached pronoun, so the doer is 'he' (third-person masculine singular) and the action is complete. The final -a is the standard past-tense vowel.

46.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
46.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

47.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
47.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

48.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
48.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.

49.meaning: A two-part word: 'and' + 'they did / worked / performed.' The verb denotes doing deeds, working, putting effort into action — practical doing as opposed to mere speaking or believing.
49.grammar: A conjunction 'wa' + a past-tense verb, 3rd person masculine plural. The -ū ending marks the subject as 'they' (a group of males or a mixed group): 'and they did / worked.'

50.meaning: 'The righteous deeds / good works' — the definite plural of a word meaning that which is sound, wholesome, upright, and beneficial. As a noun it refers to good, virtuous actions that set things right.
50.grammar: A definite sound feminine plural noun ('the good deeds'). The -i ending is the oblique case used by feminine plurals to mark either the genitive ('… of …' / after a preposition) or the accusative (direct object); for this plural pattern the accusative and genitive share the same -i ending.
50.root: ص-ل-ح (ṣ-l-ḥ) — to be sound, good, upright, set right

51.meaning: From them / among them — the preposition min ('from, out of, part of') joined to the pronoun 'them' (a group of males or a mixed group).
51.grammar: The preposition min ('from / among / part of') with the attached third-person masculine plural pronoun -hum ('them'). Pronouns after a preposition are in the genitive; the combination expresses origin, partition ('some of them'), or belonging to that group.

52.meaning: Forgiveness, pardon — the act of covering over and wiping away sins. Built on a sense of 'covering/shielding', it conveys both the concealing of faults and the remission of their consequences.
52.grammar: A verbal noun (the abstract notion of 'forgiving'). The ending -atan combines the feminine ending with the indefinite accusative marker (tanwīn). The accusative typically marks the noun as a direct object (the thing given or done), and the doubled-n sound ('nunation') signals that it is indefinite ('a/some forgiveness').

53.meaning: And a reward — in addition to the forgiveness and pleasure of Allah, the believers are promised a great reward (ʾajr ʿaẓīm — magnificent reward) for their faith and deeds.
53.grammar: Conjunction wāw + indefinite masculine noun ajr in the accusative case (manṣūb), marked by tanwīn fatḥ (-an).
53.root: أ-ج-ر (ʾ-j-r) — to reward; ajr = reward, recompense, wages

54.meaning: 'Great, immense, tremendous' — describing something vast in magnitude or weight, whether in size, importance, or seriousness.
54.grammar: An adjective ('great, immense') in an intensive pattern. The -an ending (nunation with a final alif) marks it as indefinite and in the accusative case — the case typically used for the object of a verb or for a description attached to such an object.
54.root: ع-ظ-م (ʿ-ẓ-m) — to be great, immense, mighty; greatness, a bone
